title.zh: 卷一百二十二 載記第二十二 呂光 呂纂 呂隆
title.en: Volume 122 Records 22: Lü Guang; Lü Zuan; Lü Long
title.raw: 卷一百二十二 載記第二十二 呂光 呂纂 呂隆 Volume 122 Records 22: Lü Guang; Lü Zuan; Lü Long

sentences.zh: 呂光 呂纂 呂隆

translations.literal: Lü Guang; Lü Zuan; Lü Long
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang; Lü Zuan; Lü Long

sentences.zh: 呂光，字世明，略陽氐人也。

translations.literal: Lü Guang, courtesy name Shiming, was a Di man from Lüeyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang, whose courtesy name was Shiming, came from the Di community of Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 其先呂文和，漢文帝初，自沛避難徙焉。

translations.literal: His ancestor Lü Wenhe, at the beginning of Han Wendi, from Pei fled disaster and moved there.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Lü Wenhe left Pei to escape turmoil in the early years of Emperor Wen of Han and settled there.

sentences.zh: 世為酋豪。

translations.literal: For generations they were chieftain elites.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan had been tribal magnates.

sentences.zh: 父婆樓，佐命苻堅，官至太尉。

translations.literal: Father Polou, aided the mandate of Fu Jian, office reached Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Polou had helped Fu Jian win the throne and rose to grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 光生於枋頭，夜有神光之異，故以光為名。

translations.literal: Guang was born at Fangtou; at night there was divine light anomaly; therefore took Guang as name.
translations.idiomatic: He was born at Fangtou, where a supernatural glow appeared by night, so he was given the name Guang, “radiance.”

sentences.zh: 年十歲，與諸童兒遊戲邑裏，為戰陣之法，儔類咸推為主。

translations.literal: At age ten, with various boys playing games in the village, he made battle-array methods; peers all pushed him as leader.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he organized village boys into mock battles, and every child made him commander.

sentences.zh: 部分詳平，群童嘆服。

translations.literal: Division parts detailed and fair; crowd of boys sighed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: His dispositions were fair and meticulous, and the other boys marveled.

sentences.zh: 不樂讀書，唯好鷹馬。

translations.literal: Did not delight in reading books; only loved hawks and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He cared nothing for books and lived for falconry and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺四寸，目重瞳子，左肘有肉印。

translations.literal: When grown, body eight chi four cun; eyes double pupils; left elbow had flesh seal.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he stood eight chi four cun tall, had double pupils, and bore a fleshy mark on his left elbow.

sentences.zh: 沈毅凝重，寬簡有大量，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: Deep and resolute, dignified and heavy; broad and simple had great capacity; joy and anger did not show on face.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep, steady, and imperturbable, magnanimous and unruffled, never betraying emotion.

sentences.zh: 時人莫之識也，惟王猛異之，曰：「此非常人。

translations.literal: People of the time none knew him; only Wang Meng marveled at him, saying, "This is not an ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries overlooked him, but Wang Meng said, “This is no ordinary man.”

sentences.zh: 」言之苻堅，舉賢良，除美陽令，夷夏愛服。

translations.literal: " He spoke of him to Fu Jian; recommended as worthy and good; appointed Magistrate of Meiyang; Yi and Xia loved and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended him to Fu Jian; Lü Guang was nominated as “worthy and good,” named magistrate of Meiyang, and won the affection of tribesmen and Chinese alike.

sentences.zh: 遷鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: Promoted to General Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who spreads might.

sentences.zh: 從堅征張平，戰於銅壁，刺平養子蠔，中之，自是威名大著。

translations.literal: Following Jian campaigning against Zhang Ping, battled at Tongbi, stabbed Ping's adopted son Hao, hit him; from this awesome name greatly showed.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Jian against Zhang Ping, ran him through at Tongbi, and wounded Zhang’s adopted son Hao—after that his fame spread far.

sentences.zh: 苻雙反于秦州，堅將楊成世為雙將苟興所敗，光與王鑒討之。

translations.literal: Fu Shuang rebelled in Qin Province; Jian's general Yang Chengshi was by Shuang's general Gou Xing defeated; Guang with Wang Jian campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Shuang revolted in Qin, Fu Jian’s general Yang Chengshi fell to Gou Xing; Lü Guang and Wang Jian were sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 鑒欲速戰，光曰：「興初破成世，奸氣漸張，宜持重以待其弊。

translations.literal: Jian wished quick battle; Guang said, "Xing first defeated Chengshi; treacherous spirit gradually swells—ought to hold weight to await their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian wanted a quick fight, but Lü Guang said, “Gou Xing has just routed Yang Chengshi and his arrogance is swelling—we should stand firm until he weakens.”

sentences.zh: 興乘勝輕來，糧竭必退，退而擊之，可以破也。

translations.literal: Xing riding victory lightly comes; grain exhausted must retreat; retreat then strike them—can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: He will press his luck until his supplies fail, then pull back—that is when we strike and break him.”

sentences.zh: 」二旬而興退，諸將不知所為，光曰：「揆其奸計，必攻榆眉。

translations.literal: " Twenty days then Xing retreated; generals knew not what to do; Guang said, "Measure his treacherous plan—surely attacks Yumei.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days Gou Xing withdrew; the generals hesitated until Lü Guang said, “He means to strike Yumei.”

sentences.zh: 若得榆眉，據城斷路，資儲復贍，非國之利也，宜速進師。

translations.literal: If obtains Yumei, holds city cuts road, resources and stores again abundant—not the state's benefit; ought speedily advance army.
translations.idiomatic: If he takes Yumei and blocks the road, he replenishes his stores—that hurts us. We must march at once.”

sentences.zh: 若興攻城，尤須赴救。

translations.literal: If Xing attacks city, especially must hurry to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: If he lays siege, we must relieve the place immediately.”

sentences.zh: 如其奔也，彼糧既盡，可以滅之。

translations.literal: If he flees, their grain already exhausted, can extinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: If he runs, his grain is gone and we can finish him.”

sentences.zh: 」鑒從焉。

translations.literal: " Jian followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 果敗興軍。

translations.literal: Indeed defeated Xing's army.
translations.idiomatic: They crushed Gou Xing’s army.

sentences.zh: 從王猛滅慕容暐，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: Following Wang Meng destroying Murong Wei, enfeoffed Village Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Meng in the destruction of Murong Wei and was enfeoffed as village marquis.

sentences.zh: 苻重之鎮洛陽，以光為長史。

translations.literal: When Fu Chong garrisoned Luoyang, appointed Guang as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Chong held Luoyang, Lü Guang became his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 及重謀反，苻堅聞之，曰：「呂光忠孝方正，必不同也。

translations.literal: When Chong plotted rebellion, Fu Jian heard it, said, "Lü Guang loyal, filial, upright—surely not the same.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Chong rebelled, Fu Jian said, “Lü Guang is loyal and upright—he will not join him.”

sentences.zh: 」馳使命光檻重送之。

translations.literal: " Galloping ordered Guang to casket Chong and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent urgent orders for Lü Guang to shackle Fu Chong and bring him in.

sentences.zh: 尋入為太子右率，甚見敬重。

translations.literal: Soon entered as Crown Prince's Right Leader, greatly seen respect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered court as right leader of the crown prince’s household and was held in high regard.

sentences.zh: 蜀人李焉聚眾二萬，攻逼益州。

translations.literal: Shu man Li Yan gathered a host of twenty thousand, attacked and pressed Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu man named Li Yan raised twenty thousand men and threatened Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 堅以光為破虜將軍，率兵討滅之，遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Jian appointed Guang General Who Breaks the Barbarians, led troops to campaign and destroy him, promoted to Colonel of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian named him general who breaks the barbarians; he crushed the revolt and was promoted to colonel of foot.

sentences.zh: 苻洛反，光又擊平之，拜驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Fu Luo rebelled; Guang again struck and pacified him, appointed General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He put down Fu Luo’s rebellion and was named general of valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 堅既平山東，士馬強盛，遂有圖西域之志，乃授光使持節、都督西討諸軍事，率將軍姜飛、彭晃、杜進、康盛等總兵七萬，鐵騎五千，以討西域，以隴西董方、馮翊郭抱、武威賈虔、弘農楊穎為四府佐將。

translations.literal: Jian having pacified Shandong, soldiers and horses strong and flourishing, thereupon had intent to plan the Western Regions; thereupon appointed Guang credential-bearing, commander-in-chief of all western punitive forces, leading generals Jiang Fei, Peng Huang, Du Jin, Kang Sheng, etc., total troops seventy thousand, armored cavalry five thousand, to campaign against the Western Regions; appointed Longxi Dong Fang, Fengyi Guo Bao, Wuwei Jia Qian, Hongnong Yang Ying as four headquarters assistant generals.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering the east, Fu Jian turned toward the Western Regions: he gave Lü Guang the plenipotentiary baton and command of the western expedition—seventy thousand troops including five thousand armored horse under Jiang Fei, Peng Huang, Du Jin, and Kang Sheng—with Dong Fang, Guo Bao, Jia Qian, and Yang Ying as staff generals.

sentences.zh: 堅太子宏執光手曰：「君器相非常，必有大福，宜深保愛。

translations.literal: Jian's Crown Prince Hong grasped Guang's hand saying, "Your vessel and aspect are extraordinary; surely will have great fortune; ought deeply preserve and cherish.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Fu Hong took his hand and said, “Your bearing marks you for greatness—take good care of yourself.”

sentences.zh: 」行至高昌，聞堅寇晉，光欲更須後命。

translations.literal: " Marching reaching Gaochang, heard Jian invaded Jin; Guang wished again to await later orders.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaochang he learned that Fu Jian had invaded Jin and meant to wait for new orders.

sentences.zh: 部將杜進曰：「節下受任金方，赴機宜速，有何不了，而更留乎！

translations.literal: Subordinate general Du Jin said, "Beneath your command received appointment in the metal quarter; rushing opportunity ought be swift—what is not finished, and again stay!
translations.idiomatic: Du Jin urged him: “You were sent west to seize the moment—delay serves nothing!”

sentences.zh: 」光乃進及流沙，三百餘里無水，將士失色。

translations.literal: " Guang thereupon advanced to flowing sands; three hundred-odd li without water; generals and soldiers lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang pushed into the desert, where three hundred li offered no water and his troops panicked.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「吾聞李廣利精誠玄感，飛泉湧出，吾等豈獨無感致乎！

translations.literal: Guang said, "I have heard Li Guangli's utmost sincerity mysteriously moved, flying springs gushed forth—how could we alone lack responsive attainment!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, “Li Guangli’s devotion made springs burst from the sand—are we less sincere?”

sentences.zh: 皇天必將有濟，諸君不足憂也。

translations.literal: August Heaven surely will have aid; gentlemen not worth worrying.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven will provide—there is no cause for fear.”

sentences.zh: 」俄而大雨，平地三尺。

translations.literal: " Soon great rain; flat ground three chi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a downpour left three chi of water on the flats.

sentences.zh: 進兵至焉耆，其王泥流率其旁國請降。

translations.literal: Advancing troops reached Yanqi; its king Nilü led neighboring states to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Yanqi, whose king Nilü led the neighboring states in surrender.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王帛純距光，光軍其城南，五里為一營，深溝高壘，廣設疑兵，以木為人，被之以甲，羅之壘上。

translations.literal: Kucha king Bo Chun resisted Guang; Guang armyed south of his city, five li one camp, deep moats high ramparts, broadly set doubtful troops, using wood for men, covering them with armor, arraying them on ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: King Bo Chun of Kucha defied him; Lü Guang ringed the south side with camps every five li, dug deep moats, raised high walls, and lined the parapets with armored dummies to feign strength.

sentences.zh: 帛純驅徙城外人入于城中，附庸侯王各嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Bo Chun drove and moved outside-city people into the city; vassal marquises each encircled city self-defended.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chun herded the suburban population inside while each client king held his own walls.

sentences.zh: 至是，光左臂內脈起成字，文曰「巨霸」。

translations.literal: At this, Guang's left arm inner vein rose forming characters, text said "Giant Overlord".
translations.idiomatic: Then the veins of his left arm swelled into the characters “Giant Overlord.”

sentences.zh: 營外夜有一黑物，大如斷堤，搖動有頭角，目光若電，及明而雲霧四周，遂不復見。

translations.literal: Outside camp night had a black thing, large as a cut dike, swaying had head and horns, eye light like lightning; when bright then cloud-mist four sides, then no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: A black shape as huge as a levee, horned and flashing eyes, writhed outside the camp until dawn mists swallowed it.

sentences.zh: 旦視其處，南北五里，東西三十餘步，鱗甲隱地之所，昭然猶在。

translations.literal: Dawn viewed that place; north-south five li, east-west thirty-odd steps; scale-armor pressed-ground place, clearly still there.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the ground showed scales for five li north–south and thirty paces east–west, as if a dragon had pressed there.

sentences.zh: 光笑曰：「黑龍也。

translations.literal: Guang laughed saying, "Black dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang laughed and said, “A black dragon.”

sentences.zh: 」俄而雲起西北，暴雨滅其跡。

translations.literal: " Soon clouds rose northwest; violent rain extinguished its traces.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds rose from the northwest and a cloudburst washed the traces away.

sentences.zh: 杜進言於光曰：「龍者神獸，人君利見之象。

translations.literal: Du Jin spoke to Guang saying, "Dragon is divine beast; sign of ruler's profitable seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jin said, “The dragon is a divine creature—the omen of a ruler whom Heaven favors.”

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『見龍在田，德施普也。

translations.literal: Book of Changes says: 'Dragon seen in field, virtue spreads universally.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, ‘The dragon appears in the field—his virtue spreads everywhere.’”

sentences.zh: 』斯誠明將軍道合靈和，德符幽顯。

translations.literal: ' This truly shows General's Way matches numinous harmony; virtue tallies hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this means your path joins heaven and earth and your virtue answers both realms.”

sentences.zh: 願將軍勉之，以成大慶。

translations.literal: Wish General strive for it, to complete great celebration.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to press on toward that great fortune.”

sentences.zh: 」光有喜色。

translations.literal: " Guang had joyful color.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang smiled.

sentences.zh: 又進攻龜茲城，夜夢金象飛越城外。

translations.literal: Again advanced attacking Kucha city; night dreamed golden image flying beyond city wall.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Kucha he dreamed a golden statue flew beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「此謂佛神去之，胡必亡矣。

translations.literal: Guang said, "This means Buddha spirit left; Hu must perish.
translations.idiomatic: He said, “The Buddha’s power is leaving them—the barbarians are finished.”

sentences.zh: 」光攻城既急，帛純乃傾國財寶請救獪胡。

translations.literal: " Guang attacking city already urgent; Bo Chun thereupon emptied state treasures requesting rescue from cunning Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Under heavy pressure Bo Chun spent the royal treasury hiring mercenary Hu allies.

sentences.zh: 獪胡弟呐龍、侯將馗率騎二十餘萬，並引溫宿、尉頭等國王，合七十餘萬以救之。

translations.literal: Cunning Hu younger brother Na Long, Hou general Kui led cavalry two hundred thousand-plus, together leading Wensu, Weitou, etc. country kings, totaling seven hundred thousand-plus to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Na Long, brother of the Hu chieftain, and the commander Kui brought two hundred thousand horsemen and, with the kings of Wensu, Weitou, and others, raised seven hundred thousand men to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 胡便弓馬，善矛槊，鎧如連鎖，射不可入，以革索為羂，策馬擲人，多有中者。

translations.literal: Hu skilled at bow and horse, good at spear-lance; armor like linked chains, arrows could not enter; using leather ropes as nooses, spurring horse throwing people, many hit.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled with bow and lance; their lamellar armor turned arrows; they lassoed men from the saddle and hurled them with deadly effect.

sentences.zh: 眾甚憚之。

translations.literal: The host greatly feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang’s troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸欲每營結陣，案兵以距之。

translations.literal: Generals all wished each camp form array, rest troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: His generals wanted each camp to form a separate line and wait on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「彼眾我寡，營又相遠，勢分力散，非良策也。

translations.literal: Guang said, "They many we few; camps also mutually far; situation divided strength scattered—not good strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, “They outnumber us and our camps are strung out—splitting up would be fatal.”

sentences.zh: 」於是遷營相接陣，為勾鎖之法，精騎為遊軍，彌縫其闕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon moved camps connecting arrays, made hook-lock method; picked cavalry as roaming army, stitching their gaps.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the camps into one continuous front with interlocking hooks, screened the line with picked cavalry, and plugged every weak point.

sentences.zh: 戰於城西，大敗之，斬萬餘級。

translations.literal: Battled west of city, greatly defeated them, beheaded ten thousand-plus heads.
translations.idiomatic: West of the city he routed them and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: ，帛純收其珍寶而走，王侯降者三十餘國。

translations.literal: , Bo Chun gathered his treasures and fled; kings and marquises surrendering were thirty-odd states.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chun fled with the royal treasures, and more than thirty kingdoms submitted.

sentences.zh: 光入其城，大饗將士，賦詩言志。

translations.literal: Guang entered his city, greatly feasted generals and soldiers, composed poems stating intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang entered Kucha, feasted his army, and composed verse to voice his ambition.

sentences.zh: 見其宮室壯麗，命參軍京兆段業著《龜茲宮賦》以譏之。

translations.literal: Seeing its palaces grand and beautiful, ordered aide Jingzhao Duan Ye compose "Rhapsody on Kucha Palace" to satirize it.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by the opulence of the palace, he ordered his aide Duan Ye of Jingzhao to compose “Rhapsody on the Kucha Palace” in mockery.

sentences.zh: 胡人奢侈，厚於養生，家有蒲桃酒，或至千斛，經十年不敗，士卒淪沒酒藏者相繼矣。

translations.literal: Hu people extravagant, thick in nurturing life; households had grape wine, some reached thousand hu; passing ten years not spoiled; soldiers drowned in wine stores succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu lived in luxury—some cellars held a thousand hu of wine that kept ten years—and Lü Guang’s men drowned themselves in it one after another.

sentences.zh: 諸國憚光威名，貢款屬路，乃立帛純弟震為王以安之。

translations.literal: Various states feared Guang's awesome name; tribute and sincerity lined the roads; thereupon established Bo Chun's younger brother Zhen as king to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The states, awed by his name, sent tribute along every road; he enthroned Bo Chun’s brother Zhen to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 光撫寧西域，威恩甚著，桀黠胡王昔所未賓者，不遠萬里皆來歸附，上漢所賜節傳，光皆表而易之。

translations.literal: Guang soothed and pacified Western Regions; might and grace very manifest; fierce-cunning Hu kings formerly not guested, not far ten thousand li all came to attach, presenting Han-granted credentials; Guang all memorialized and exchanged them.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled the Western Regions with a blend of awe and kindness until even defiant kings crossed thousands of li to submit, handing over Han credentials for ones he issued by memorial to the court.

sentences.zh: 堅聞光平西域，以為使持節、散騎常侍、都督玉門已西諸軍事，安西將軍、西域校尉，道絕不通。

translations.literal: Jian heard Guang pacified Western Regions, appointed him credential-bearing, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, commander-in-chief of all military affairs west of Jade Gate, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Western Regions; road cut not connected.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian promoted him to plenipotentiary, cavalier attendant, commander west of the Jade Gate, general who pacifies the west, and colonel of the Western Regions—but the route was severed and the patent never reached him.

sentences.zh: 光既平龜茲，有留焉之志。

translations.literal: Guang having pacified Kucha, had intent to remain there.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Kucha he considered staying in the west.

sentences.zh: 時始獲鳩摩羅什，羅什勸之東還，語在《西夷傳》。

translations.literal: At the time first captured Kumarajiva; Kumarajiva urged him east return; words are in "Western Yi Biography".
translations.idiomatic: He had just captured Kumarajiva, who urged him to march east—the account is in the “Treatise on the Western Barbarians.”

sentences.zh: 光於是大饗文武，博議進止。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon greatly feasted civil and military, broadly deliberated advance and stop.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his officers and debated whether to advance or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 眾咸請還，光從之，以駝二萬餘頭致外國珍寶及奇伎異戲、殊禽怪獸千有餘品，駿馬萬餘匹。

translations.literal: Host all requested return; Guang followed it; using camels twenty thousand-plus heads carried foreign treasures and strange skills different entertainments, rare birds and odd beasts thousand-odd kinds, fine horses ten thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: They voted to return; Lü Guang agreed and loaded more than twenty thousand camels with foreign treasure, acrobats, exotic beasts, and over ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 而苻堅高昌太守楊翰說其涼州刺史梁熙距守高桐、伊吾二關，熙不從。

translations.literal: But Fu Jian's Gaochang Administrator Yang Han persuaded his Liang Province Inspector Liang Xi to hold and defend Gao Tong and Yiwu two passes; Xi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian’s governor of Gaochang, Yang Han, urged Liang Xi to block the Gao Tong and Yiwu passes; Liang Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 光至高昌，翰以郡迎降。

translations.literal: Guang reached Gaochang; Han with the commandery welcomed and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang reached Gaochang, Yang Han surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，光聞翰之說，惡之，又聞苻堅喪敗，長安危逼，謀欲停師。

translations.literal: Initially, Guang heard Han's plan, loathed it; again heard Fu Jian defeated, Chang'an peril pressed; plotted wishing to halt army.
translations.idiomatic: He had resented Yang Han’s advice, and when he heard of Fu Jian’s defeat and Chang’an’s peril he thought of halting.

sentences.zh: 杜進諫曰：「梁熙文雅有餘，機鑒不足，終不能納善從說也，願不足憂之。

translations.literal: Du Jin remonstrated saying, "Liang Xi cultured elegance has surplus, keen insight lacks; in the end cannot accept good follow advice—wish not worth worrying.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jin said, “Liang Xi is cultured but dull—he will never heed good counsel; do not fret.”

sentences.zh: 聞其上下未同，宜在速進，進而不捷，請受過言之誅。

translations.literal: Hear his high and low not united; ought be in swift advance; advance and not succeed, request receive excessive-speech execution.
translations.idiomatic: His court is divided—strike now; if we fail, execute me for rash words.”

sentences.zh: 」光從之。

translations.literal: " Guang followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang agreed.

sentences.zh: 及至玉門，梁熙傳檄責光擅命還師，遣子胤與振威姚皓、別駕衛翰率眾五萬，距光於灑泉。

translations.literal: When reached Jade Gate, Liang Xi circulated proclamation blaming Guang usurping orders returning army, sent son Yin with General Who Shakes Might Yao Hao, Aide Wei Han leading host fifty thousand, resisting Guang at Shaiquan.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jade Gate, Liang Xi accused Lü Guang of returning without orders and sent his son Liang Yin with Yao Hao and Wei Han and fifty thousand men to oppose him near Jiuquan (the manuscript reads Shaiquan).

sentences.zh: 光報檄涼州，責熙無赴難之誠，數其遏歸師之罪。

translations.literal: Guang returned proclamation to Liang Province, blamed Xi for lacking rush-to-calamity sincerity, counted his crime of blocking returning army.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang answered with a manifesto denouncing Liang Xi for failing to aid the throne and for blocking a loyal army’s return.

sentences.zh: 遣彭晃、杜進、姜飛等為前鋒，擊胤，大敗之。

translations.literal: Sent Peng Huang, Du Jin, Jiang Fei, etc. as vanguard, struck Yin, greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Peng Huang, Du Jin, and Jiang Fei against Liang Yin and shattered him.

sentences.zh: 胤輕將麾下數百騎東奔，杜進追擒之。

translations.literal: Yin lightly led several hundred cavalry of his command east fleeing; Du Jin pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yin fled east with a few hundred horse; Du Jin ran him down and took him.

sentences.zh: 於是四山胡夷皆來款附。

translations.literal: Thereupon four mountains Hu and Yi all came to offer attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes from every quarter then pledged allegiance.

sentences.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙請降。

translations.literal: Wuwei Administrator Peng Ji seized Xi requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ji, governor of Wuwei, seized Liang Xi and offered submission.

sentences.zh: 光入姑臧，自領涼州刺史、護羌校尉，表杜進為輔國將軍、武威太守，封武始侯，自余封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Guang entered Guzang, personally concurrent Liang Province Inspector, Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, memorialized Du Jin as General Who Aids the State, Wuwei Administrator, enfeoffed Marquis of Wushi; the rest enfeoffments each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang took Guzang, added the titles of inspector of Liang and colonel who protects the Qiang, memorialized Du Jin as general who aids the state and marquis of Wushi, governor of Wuwei, and distributed other ranks as deserved.

sentences.zh: 光主簿尉祐，奸佞傾薄人也，見棄前朝，與彭齊同謀執梁熙，光深見寵任，乃譖誅南安姚皓、天水尹景等名士十餘人，遠近頗以此離貳。

translations.literal: Guang's registrar Wei You, treacherous flatterer fickle man, seen discarded former court, with Peng Qi together plotted seizing Liang Xi; Guang deeply saw favor and trust; thereupon slandered and executed Nan'an Yao Hao, Tianshui Yin Jing, etc. eminent gentlemen ten-odd persons; far and near somewhat thereby split allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei You, Lü Guang’s registrar, was a sycophant cast off by the previous regime; he had helped Peng Qi seize Liang Xi and now won Lü Guang’s trust, then slandered more than a dozen worthy men such as Yao Hao of Nan’an and Yin Jing of Tianshui into execution, alienating many near and far.

sentences.zh: 光尋擢祐為甯遠將軍、金城太守。

translations.literal: Guang soon promoted You to General Who Pacifies the Distance, Jincheng Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lü Guang raised Wei You to general who pacifies the distance and governor of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 祐次允吾，襲據外城以叛，祐從弟隨據鸇陰以應之。

translations.literal: You halted at Yunwu, raided and held outer city to rebel; You's cousin Sui held Zanyin to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wei You stopped at Yunwu, seized the outer city in revolt, and his cousin Wei Sui held Zanyin in support.

sentences.zh: 光遣其將魏真討隨，隨敗，奔祐，光將姜飛又擊敗祐眾。

translations.literal: Guang sent his general Wei Zhen to campaign against Sui; Sui defeated, fled to You; Guang's general Jiang Fei again struck and defeated You's host.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent Wei Zhen against Wei Sui; Sui fled to Wei You, and Jiang Fei crushed their forces.

sentences.zh: 祐奔據興城，扇動百姓，夷夏多從之。

translations.literal: You fled and held Xingcheng, fanned and moved hundred surnames; Yi and Xia many followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei You fell back to Xingcheng, stirred up the people, and drew many tribesmen and Chinese to his banner.

sentences.zh: 飛司馬張象、參軍郭雅謀殺飛應祐，發覺，逃奔。

translations.literal: Fei's Major Zhang Xiang, Aide Guo Ya plotted killing Fei to respond to You; discovered; fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fei’s major Zhang Xiang and aide Guo Ya plotted to kill him for Wei You; exposed, they fled.

sentences.zh: 初，苻堅之敗，張天錫南奔，其世子大豫為長水校尉王穆所匿。

translations.literal: Initially, when Fu Jian was defeated, Zhang Tianxi south fled; his heir-apparent Dayu was by Colonel of Chang Waters Wang Mu hidden.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian’s defeat Zhang Tianxi fled south, and his heir Zhang Dayu was hidden by Wang Mu, colonel of the Chang River.

sentences.zh: 及堅還長安，穆將大豫奔禿髮思復犍，思復犍送之魏安。

translations.literal: When Jian returned Chang'an, Mu led Dayu fled to Tufa Sigujian; Sigujian sent him to Weian.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian returned to Chang’an, Wang Mu took Zhang Dayu to Tufa Sigujian, who sent them on to Weian.

sentences.zh: 是月，魏安人焦松、齊肅、張濟等起兵數千，迎大豫於揟次，陷昌松郡。

translations.literal: That month, Weian men Jiao Song, Qi Su, Zhang Ji, etc. raised troops several thousand, welcomed Dayu at Zuci, took Changsong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jiao Song, Qi Su, and Zhang Ji of Weian raised several thousand men, welcomed Zhang Dayu at Zuci, and seized Changsong commandery.

sentences.zh: 光遣其將杜進討之，為大豫聽敗。

translations.literal: Guang sent his general Du Jin to campaign against them; was by Dayu heard defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent Du Jin, who suffered defeat at Zhang Dayu’s hands.

sentences.zh: 大豫遂進逼姑臧，求決勝負，王穆諫曰：「呂光糧豐城固，甲兵精銳，逼之非利。

translations.literal: Dayu thereupon advanced pressing Guzang, sought deciding victory-defeat; Wang Mu remonstrated saying, "Lü Guang grain abundant city solid, armor and weapons keen—pressing him not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dayu pressed on to Guzang demanding battle; Wang Mu warned, “Lü Guang has ample grain, strong walls, and crack troops—forcing a fight helps us not.”

sentences.zh: 不如席捲嶺西，厲兵積粟，東向而爭，不及期年，可以平也。

translations.literal: Better roll-mat west of ranges, sharpen troops pile grain, eastward contend; not reaching full year, can pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Better sweep the lands west of the ranges, train troops, and store grain, then strike east—within a year we can win.”

sentences.zh: 」大豫不從，乃遣穆求救于嶺西諸郡，建康太守李隰、祁連都尉嚴純及閻襲起兵應之。

translations.literal: " Dayu did not follow; thereupon sent Mu to seek rescue from west-of-range commanderies; Jiankang Administrator Li Xi, Qilian Commandant Yan Chun, and Yan Xi raised troops responding to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dayu refused and sent Wang Mu to beg help from the commanderies west of the ranges; Li Xi, governor of Jiankang, Yan Chun, commandant of Qilian, and Yan Xi rose in his support.

sentences.zh: 大豫進屯城西，王穆率眾三萬及思復犍子奚于等陣于城南。

translations.literal: Dayu advanced and encamped west of the city; Wang Mu led thirty thousand troops together with Xi Yu, son of Sifu Jian, and others, and drew up battle lines south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dayu shifted his camp to the west of the city while Wang Mu brought thirty thousand men plus Xi Yu, son of Sifu Jian, and others to form ranks south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 光出擊，破之，斬奚于等二萬餘級。

translations.literal: Guang went out and struck them, defeated them, and beheaded Xi Yu and the rest to a count of more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sallied forth, broke their lines, and took over twenty thousand heads, including Xi Yu and his followers.

sentences.zh: 光謂諸將曰：「大豫若用王穆之言，恐未可平也。

translations.literal: Guang said to the generals, "If Dayu had used Wang Mu's words, perhaps he could not have been pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang told his officers, "Had Dayu heeded Wang Mu's counsel, we might never have subdued him."

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「大豫豈不及此邪！

translations.literal: The generals said, "How could Dayu not reach this!"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Surely Dayu was not blind to that!"

sentences.zh: 皇天欲贊成明公八百之業，故令大豫迷於良算耳。

translations.literal: August Heaven wished to assist in completing the enlightened lord's enterprise of eight hundred years, therefore caused Dayu to be confused about sound plans.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven means to secure your long reign, so it muddled Dayu's judgment and kept him from wise strategy.

sentences.zh: 」光大悅，賜金帛有差。

translations.literal: Guang was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang was delighted and distributed gold and silk according to rank.

sentences.zh: 大豫自西郡詣臨洮，驅略百姓五千餘戶，保據俱城。

translations.literal: Dayu went from Xijun to Lintao, drove off and plundered more than five thousand households of commoners, and held fast at Jucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dayu marched from Xijun to Lintao, seized over five thousand civilian households, and fortified himself at Jucheng.

sentences.zh: 光將彭晃、徐炅攻破之，大豫奔廣武，穆奔建康。

translations.literal: Guang's generals Peng Huang and Xu Jiong attacked and broke them; Dayu fled to Guangwu, and Mu fled to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Peng Huang and Xu Jiong crushed their position; Dayu bolted for Guangwu and Wang Mu for Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 廣武人執大豫，送之，斬于姑臧市。

translations.literal: The people of Guangwu seized Dayu, sent him in, and beheaded him in the market of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangwu captured Dayu, turned him over, and he was executed in the marketplace at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 光至是始聞苻堅為姚萇所害，奮怒哀號，三軍縞素，大臨于城南，偽諡堅曰文昭皇帝，長吏百石已上服斬縗三月，庶人哭泣三日。

translations.literal: Only then did Guang hear that Fu Jian had been harmed by Yao Chang; he roused anger and wailed; the three armies wore white; they held a great mourning south of the city; he falsely posthumously titled Jian as Emperor Wenzhao; officials of one hundred shi and above wore hemp mourning three months; commoners wept three days.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang learned only then that Fu Jian had been killed by Yao Chang. Shaken by grief and rage, he had the army dress in mourning and staged a grand lamentation south of the city. He posthumously honored Fu Jian as Emperor Wenzhao; officials at one hundred shi and above observed the deepest mourning for three months, and commoners were to weep for three days.

sentences.zh: 光於是大赦境內，建元曰太安，自稱使持節、侍中、中外大都督、督隴右河西諸軍事、大將軍、鄰護匈奴中郎將、涼州牧、酒泉公。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon greatly amnestied within the borders, established the era name Tai'an, and styled himself Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, Palace Attendant, Grand Commander over Court and Field, Area Commander for military affairs of Longyou and Hexi, Grand General, concurrently General of the Gentlemen of the Household Who Protects the Xiongnu, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the reign title Tai'an, and took the titles Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, Palace Attendant, Grand Commander over Court and Field, Area Commander for Longyou and Hexi, Grand General, concurrent General of the Gentlemen of the Household Who Protects the Xiongnu, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 王穆襲據酒泉，自稱大將軍、涼州牧。

translations.literal: Wang Mu seized and occupied Jiuquan, styling himself Grand General and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu struck, seized Jiuquan, and proclaimed himself Grand General and Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 時穀價踴貴，斗直五百，人相食，死者太半。

translations.literal: At the time grain prices leaped high; one dou was worth five hundred cash; people ate one another; the dead were more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Grain soared to five hundred cash a peck; people turned to cannibalism, and more than half of them perished.

sentences.zh: 光西平太守康寧自稱匈奴王，阻兵以叛，光屢遣討之，不捷。

translations.literal: Guang's Xiping prefect Kang Ning styled himself King of the Xiongnu, blocked troops and rebelled; Guang repeatedly sent forces to attack him, without success.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Ning, prefect of Xiping under Lü Guang, declared himself king of the Xiongnu and rose in arms. Lü Guang sent repeated expeditions but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 初，光之定河西也，杜進有力焉，以為輔國將軍、武威太守。

translations.literal: Initially, when Guang had settled Hexi, Du Jin had strength therein; he appointed him Support-of-the-State General and Wuwei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Du Jin had been instrumental when Lü Guang secured Hexi, so Guang named him Support the State General and governor of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 既居都尹，權高一時，出入羽儀，與光相亞。

translations.literal: Having occupied the capital intendant post, his authority was high for a time; in and out he had feathered banners, ranking second only to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the capital magistracy, his power rivaled the throne: his retinue matched Lü Guang's in splendor.

sentences.zh: 光甥石聰至自關中，光曰：「中州人言吾政化何如？

translations.literal: Guang's nephew Shi Cong arrived from Guanzhong; Guang said, "What do the Central Plain people say of my governance and transformation?"
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Shi Cong arrived from the Guanzhong region, and Lü Guang asked, "What do people in the heartland say of my rule?"

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「止知有杜進耳，實不聞有舅。

translations.literal: Cong said, "They only know there is Du Jin; truly they have not heard of an uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong replied, "They speak only of Du Jin; I barely hear anyone mention you, Uncle."

sentences.zh: 」光默然，因此誅進。

translations.literal: Guang was silent; therefore he executed Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang fell silent and on that account put Du Jin to death.

sentences.zh: 光後宴群僚，酒酣，語及政事。

translations.literal: Later Guang feasted the host of officials; when the wine was deep, they spoke of government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet for his officials, as the wine flowed the talk turned to government.

sentences.zh: 時刑法峻重，參軍段業進曰：「嚴刑重憲，非明王之義也。

translations.literal: At the time punishments were harsh and heavy; adjutant Duan Ye advanced and said, "Severe punishments and heavy statutes are not the meaning of an enlightened king."
translations.idiomatic: The laws were crushingly harsh. Staff officer Duan Ye spoke up: "Draconian penalties are not the way of a wise ruler."

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「商鞅之法至峻，而兼諸侯；

translations.literal: Guang said, "Shang Yang's laws reached harshness, yet he annexed the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang answered, "Shang Yang's code was extremely severe, yet Qin swallowed the feudal states;

sentences.zh: 吳起之術無親，而荊蠻以霸，何也？

translations.literal: Wu Qi's methods had no kinship, yet the Jing Man thereby hegemonized; why?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qi showed no mercy to kin, yet Chu rose to hegemony among the southern tribes. Why was that?

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「明公受天眷命，方君臨四海，景行堯、舜，猶懼有弊，奈何欲以商、申之末法臨道義之神州，豈此州士女所望於明公哉！

translations.literal: Ye said, "The enlightened lord has received Heaven's favoring mandate, is about to lord over the four seas, should model conduct after Yao and Shun, and still fear fault; how then wish to use Shang Yang and Shen Buhai's final methods to face the divine continent of the Way and righteousness; is this what the gentlemen and ladies of this province hope from the enlightened lord!"
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye replied, "You bear Heaven's mandate and aim to rule all under heaven. Even emulating Yao and Shun, you should fear missteps. How could you govern this heartland of civilization with the harsh expedients of Shang Yang and Shen Buhai? Is that what the people of Liangzhou expect from you?"

sentences.zh: 」光改容謝之，於是下令責躬，及崇寬簡之政。

translations.literal: Guang changed countenance and apologized to him; thereupon issued orders blaming himself, and promoted broad and simple government.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang's manner changed and he apologized, then issued an edict of self-reproach and pledged to pursue lenient, sparing rule.

sentences.zh: 其將徐炅與張掖太守彭晃謀叛，光遣師討炅，炅奔晃。

translations.literal: His general Xu Jiong and Zhangye prefect Peng Huang plotted rebellion; Guang dispatched troops to attack Jiong; Jiong fled to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: General Xu Jiong conspired with Peng Huang, prefect of Zhangye. Lü Guang sent a force against Xu Jiong, who fled to Peng Huang.

sentences.zh: 晃東結康寧，四通王穆，光議將討之，諸將咸曰：「今康寧在南，阻兵伺隙，若大駕西行，寧必乘虛出於嶺左。

translations.literal: Huang linked with Kang Ning to the east and coordinated in four directions with Wang Mu; Guang deliberated attacking them; the generals all said, "Now Kang Ning is in the south, blocks troops and watches for openings; if the great chariot goes west, Ning must seize the void and emerge left of the ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Huang allied eastward with Kang Ning and coordinated with Wang Mu on every side. When Lü Guang proposed a campaign, his generals objected: "Kang Ning holds the south and watches for an opening. If the main host marches west, he will surely slip through the passes on our left while we are away.

sentences.zh: 晃、穆未平，康寧復至，進退狼狽，勢必大危。

translations.literal: Huang and Mu not yet pacified, Kang Ning again arrives; advance and retreat are in dire straits; the situation must be greatly perilous.
translations.idiomatic: With Peng Huang and Wang Mu still unbeaten, Kang Ning would strike as well; we would be caught between forces and face disaster.

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「事勢實如卿言。

translations.literal: Guang said, "The situation of affairs truly is as you say.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, "Your reading of the field is sound.

sentences.zh: 今而不往，尋坐待其來。

translations.literal: Now if we do not go, soon we sit waiting for them to come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we stay put, we will only wait for them to close in.

sentences.zh: 晃、穆共相脣齒，寧又同惡相救，東西交至，城外非吾之有，若是，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Huang and Mu together are lip and teeth; Ning again is the same evil and mutually aids; east and west both arrive; outside the city is not ours; if thus, the great matter is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Huang and Wang Mu shield each other like lips and teeth, and Kang Ning will aid his fellow rebels. Attacks from east and west together would leave us holding only the walls, and the cause would be lost.

sentences.zh: 今晃叛逆始爾，甯、穆與之情契未密，及其倉卒，取之為易。

translations.literal: Now Huang's rebellion has only just begun; Ning's and Mu's bond with him in feeling is not yet close; catch them in haste, and taking them is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Huang has only just rebelled; his understanding with Kang Ning and Wang Mu is still shallow. We should strike while they are unprepared; victory will come more easily.

sentences.zh: 且隆替命也，卿勿復言。

translations.literal: Moreover rise and fall is fate; you need not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Rise and fall are Heaven's decree. Say no more.

sentences.zh: 」光於是自率步騎三萬，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon personally led thirty thousand foot and horse, doubling the road and marching together.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 既至，攻之二旬，晃將寇顗斬關納光，於是誅彭晃。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he attacked twenty days; Huang's general Kou Yi cut the pass and admitted Guang; thereupon he executed Peng Huang.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days of siege, Kou Yi, a subordinate of Peng Huang, opened the gates to Lü Guang. Peng Huang was then executed.

sentences.zh: 王穆以其党索嘏為敦煌太守，既而忌其威名，率眾攻嘏。

translations.literal: Wang Mu used his partisan Suo Gu as Dunhuang prefect; afterward he envied his prestige and name, and led the crowd to attack Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu had appointed his follower Suo Gu as governor of Dunhuang, then grew jealous of his growing renown and led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 光聞之，謂諸將曰：「二虜相攻，此成擒也。

translations.literal: Guang heard it and said to the generals, "The two enemies attack each other; this is ready capture.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang heard this, he told his officers, "Those two foes are clawing at each other; this hands us an easy capture.

sentences.zh: 」光將攻之，眾咸以為不可。

translations.literal: Guang was about to attack them; the crowd all thought it not possible.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared to march, but his commanders all thought it unwise.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「取亂侮亡，武之善經，不可以累征之勞而失永逸之舉。

translations.literal: Guang said, "Taking chaos and insulting destruction is the good constant of war; one cannot because of accumulated campaigns' labor lose one stroke of lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang replied, "Exploiting turmoil and finishing a failing foe is the essence of war. We must not shun repeated expeditions and forfeit a chance at lasting peace."

sentences.zh: 」率步騎二萬攻酒泉，克之，進次涼興。

translations.literal: He led twenty thousand foot and horse, attacked Jiuquan, overcame it, and advanced to station at Liangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He took twenty thousand infantry and cavalry, seized Jiuquan, and advanced to camp at Liangxing.

sentences.zh: 穆引師東還，路中眾散，穆單騎奔騂馬，騂馬令郭文斬首送之。

translations.literal: Mu led troops east back; on the road the crowd scattered; Mu on a single horse fled to Zuoma; the Zuoma magistrate Guo Wen beheaded him and sent the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu withdrew eastward, but his men melted away on the road. He fled alone to Zuoma, where Magistrate Guo Wen struck off his head and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 是時麟見金澤縣，百獸從之，光以為已瑞，以孝武太元十四年僭即三河王位，置百官自丞郎已下，赦其境內，年號麟嘉。

translations.literal: At this time a qilin appeared in Jinze county, and a hundred beasts followed it; Guang took it as an omen for himself; in Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan fourteenth year he usurped ascended the Three Rivers king title, set hundred officials from assistant gentlemen down, amnestied within the borders, and era name Linjia.
translations.idiomatic: A qilin was sighted in Jinze County, with many beasts trailing behind. Lü Guang took it as his own sign. In the fourteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, he assumed the title King of Sanhe without authority, installed a full bureaucracy down to secretaries and gentlemen, declared an amnesty, and adopted the reign title Linjia.

sentences.zh: 光妻石氏、子紹、弟德世至自仇池，光迎於城東，大饗群臣。

translations.literal: Guang's wife the Shi clan, son Shao, and brother Deshi arrived from Chouchi; Guang welcomed them east of the city and greatly feasted the host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Shi, his son Lü Shao, and his brother Deshi arrived from Chouchi. Lü Guang received them east of the city and held a grand banquet for his officials.

sentences.zh: 遣其子左將軍他、武賁中郎將纂討北虜匹勤於三岩山，大破之。

translations.literal: He sent his son Left General Ta and Brave-Gentlemen Household General Zuan to attack the northern barbarian Pi Qin at Sanyan Mountain, and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his son Ta, General of the Left, and Zuan, General of the Household Gentlemen Rapid as Tigers, to campaign against the northern foe Pi Qin at Mount Sanyan and routed him soundly.

sentences.zh: 立妻石氏為王妃，子紹為世子。

translations.literal: He established wife Shi as royal consort and son Shao as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Shi his queen and Lü Shao crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宴其群臣于內苑新堂。

translations.literal: He feasted his host of officials in the inner park's new hall.
translations.idiomatic: He entertained his ministers in the New Hall of the inner gardens.

sentences.zh: 太廟新成，追尊其高祖為敬公，曾祖為恭公，祖為宣公，父為景昭王，母曰昭烈妃。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple was newly completed; he posthumously honored his high ancestor as Duke Jing, great-great-grand as Duke Gong, grandfather as Duke Xuan, father as King Jingzhao, and mother as Consort Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic temple was newly finished. He gave posthumous titles to his ancestors: his remote forebear as Duke Jing, the next as Duke Gong, his grandfather as Duke Xuan, his father as King Jingzhao, and his mother as Consort Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 其中書侍郎楊穎上疏，請依三代故事，追尊呂望為始祖，永為不遷之廟，光從之。

translations.literal: Among them Central Secretariat Gentleman Yang Ying submitted a memorial, requesting according to Three Dynasties precedent to posthumously honor Lü Wang as first ancestor, eternally as a non-moved temple; Guang followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Secretariat Yang Ying proposed following the precedent of the Three Dynasties to enshrine Lü Wang as primordial ancestor and grant him a permanent, unmoving temple rank. Lü Guang agreed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，張掖督郵傅曜考核屬縣，而丘池令尹興殺之，投諸空井，曜見夢於光曰：「臣張掖郡小吏，案校諸縣，而丘池令尹興贓狀狼藉，懼臣言之，殺臣投于南亭空井中。

translations.literal: That year, Zhangye supervising mail Fu Yao inspected the dependent counties, but Qiuchi magistrate Yin Xing killed him and threw him into an empty well; Yao appeared in a dream to Guang and said, "Your subject is a petty clerk of Zhangye prefecture; I investigated the various counties, but Qiuchi magistrate Yin Xing's corrupt appearance was in disorder; he feared your subject speaking it, killed your subject, and threw me in the south pavilion's empty well.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fu Yao, the postal inspector of Zhangye, was reviewing the subordinate counties when Magistrate Yin Xing of Qiuchi murdered him and cast the body into a dry well. Fu Yao appeared to Lü Guang in a dream and said, "I was a minor clerk of Zhangye inspecting the counties. Yin Xing of Qiuchi, awash with evidence of corruption, feared my report, killed me, and threw me into the empty well south of the post station.

sentences.zh: 臣衣服形狀如是。

translations.literal: Your subject's garments and form are like this.
translations.idiomatic: These were my clothes and how I looked.

sentences.zh: 」光寤而猶見，久之乃滅。

translations.literal: Guang woke and still saw him; after a long time then he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang woke but still saw the apparition; only after a long while did it fade.

sentences.zh: 遣使覆之如夢，光怒，殺興。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to investigate like the dream; Guang was angry and killed Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to verify the account, and it matched the dream. Enraged, he executed Yin Xing.

sentences.zh: 著作郎段業以光未能揚清激濁，使賢愚殊貫，因療疾於天梯山，作表志詩《九歎》、《七諷》十六篇以諷焉。

translations.literal: Editorial Director Duan Ye because Guang could not raise the clear and excite the turbid, causing worthy and foolish to have separate grades, therefore treated illness at Tianti Mountain, composed expressing-intent poems "Nine Laments" and "Seven Admonitions" in sixteen pieces to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial Director Duan Ye thought Lü Guang had failed to sort the worthy from the base, so he retired to Mount Tianti to convalesce and wrote sixteen didactic poems, including the "Nine Sighs" and "Seven Satires," to remonstrate with him.

sentences.zh: 光覽而悅之。

translations.literal: Guang read them and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang read them with satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 南羌彭奚念入攻白土，都尉孫峙退奔興城。

translations.literal: The southern Qiang Peng Xinian entered and attacked Baitu; Commandant Sun Zhi retreated and fled to Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Xinian of the southern Qiang struck Baitu, driving Commandant Sun Zhi back toward Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 光遣其南中郎將呂方及其弟右將軍呂寶、振威楊范、強弩竇苟討乞伏乾歸於金城。

translations.literal: Guang sent his South General of the Gentlemen Lü Fang and his brother Right General Lü Bao, Shake-the-Awesome Yang Fan, and Strong Crossbow Dou Gou to attack Qifu Qian Gui at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lü Fang, General of the Gentlemen of the South, with his brother Lü Bao, General of the Right, along with Yang Fan who bore the title that shook the foe, and crossbow commander Dou Gou, to campaign against Qifu Qian Gui at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 方屯河北，寶進師濟河，為乾歸所敗，寶死之。

translations.literal: Fang encamped north of the river; Bao advanced the army across the river, was defeated by Qian Gui, and Bao died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fang held the north bank while Lü Bao crossed the river, was defeated by Qian Gui, and died in the fight.

sentences.zh: 武賁呂篡、強弩竇苟率步騎五千南討彭奚念，戰於盤夷，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Brave Lü Cuan and Strong Crossbow Dou Gou led five thousand foot and horse south to attack Peng Xinian, battled at Panyi, were greatly defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Cuan of the Rapid Tigers and Dou Gou led five thousand foot and horse south against Peng Xinian, fought at Panyi, and retreated in shambles.

sentences.zh: 光親討乾歸、奚念，遣纂及揚武楊軌、建忠沮渠羅仇、建武梁恭軍于左南。

translations.literal: Guang personally attacked Qian Gui and Xinian; he sent Zuan and Shake-the-Military Yang Gui, Establish-Loyalty Juqu Luochou, and Establish-Warfare Liang Gong to encamp at Zuonan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang took the field in person against Qian Gui and Xinian, sending Zuan with Yang Gui who bore the title that displayed martial might, Juqu Luochou who bore the loyal bulwark title, and Liang Gong who bore the martial establishment title, to encamp at Zuonan.

sentences.zh: 奚念大懼，于白土津累石為堤，以水自固，遣精兵一萬距守河津。

translations.literal: Xinian was greatly afraid; at the Baitu ford he piled stone as a dike, used water to fortify himself, and sent ten thousand crack troops to resist and guard the river ford.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xinian piled stones into a levee at the Baitu ford to shield himself with the river and posted ten thousand picked troops to hold the crossing.

sentences.zh: 光遣將軍王寶潛趣上津，夜渡湟河。

translations.literal: Guang sent General Wang Bao secretly to hurry to Shangjin and cross the Huang River by night.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Wang Bao to slip upstream toward the upper ford and cross the Huangshui by night.

sentences.zh: 光濟自石堤，攻克枹罕，奚念單騎奔甘松，光振旅而旋。

translations.literal: Guang crossed from the stone dike, attacked and took Fuhan; Xinian on a single horse fled to Gansong; Guang shook the troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang forded at the stone weir, stormed Fuhan, and sent Xinian fleeing alone toward Gansong before marching home in good order.

sentences.zh: 初，光徙西海郡人于諸郡，至是，謠曰：「朔馬心何悲？

translations.literal: Initially, Guang had moved the people of Xihai commandery to various commanderies; arriving at this, a ballad said, "North horses' hearts how sad?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lü Guang had resettled the people of Xihai commandery to other jurisdictions. Then a rhyme spread: "Why do the northern horses grieve,

sentences.zh: 念舊中心勞。

translations.literal: Thinking of the old, the center toils.
translations.idiomatic: remembering their old homes, their hearts grow weary—

sentences.zh: 燕雀何徘徊？

translations.literal: Swallows and sparrows why linger?
translations.idiomatic: Why do the swallows and sparrows hover,

sentences.zh: 意欲還故巢。

translations.literal: Their intent desires to return to the old nest.
translations.idiomatic: They only wish to return to their old nests.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，遂相扇動，復徙之于西河樂都。

translations.literal: Soon, then they mutually fanned and moved; he again moved them to Xihe Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the mood spread unrest, so he moved them again to Ledu in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 群議以高昌雖在西垂，地居形勝，外接胡虜，易生翻覆，宜遣子弟鎮之。

translations.literal: Group deliberation held that although Gaochang was on the western edge, its land occupied strategic terrain, outside it connected to Hu barbarians, easy to produce overturn; it was fitting to send sons and younger brothers to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: His advisers argued that Gaochang, though on the far western edge, occupied key ground and bordered non-Chinese peoples, inviting revolt; princes or sons should be posted there.

sentences.zh: 光以子覆為使持節、鎮西將軍、都督玉門已西諸軍事、西域大都護，鎮高昌，命大臣子弟隨之。

translations.literal: Guang used son Fu as Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, Garrison-the-West General, Area Commander for military affairs west of Yumen and beyond, Grand Protector of the Western Regions, garrisoned Gaochang, and ordered great ministers' sons and younger brothers to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his son Fu Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, General Who Guards the West, Area Commander for all military matters west of Yumen, and Grand Protector of the Western Regions, stationing him at Gaochang with the sons of leading families in his train.

sentences.zh: 光於是乙太元二十一年僭即天王位，大赦境內，改年龍飛。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon in Taiyuan twenty-first year usurped ascended the Heavenly King position, greatly amnestied within the borders, and changed the year to Longfei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Taiyuan era he then assumed the title of Heavenly King without Jin's leave, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Longfei.

sentences.zh: 立世子紹為太子，諸子弟為公侯者二十人。

translations.literal: He established heir apparent Shao as crown prince; twenty of the various sons and younger brothers became dukes or marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated heir Lü Shao to crown prince and ennobled twenty younger kinsmen as dukes or marquises.

sentences.zh: 中書令王詳為尚書左僕射，段業等五人為尚書。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Wang Xiang became Minister Left Assistant; Duan Ye and five others became Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang was promoted from Director of the Secretariat to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duan Ye plus four others became ministers.

sentences.zh: 乾歸從弟軻彈來奔，光下書曰：「乾歸狼子野心，前後反覆。

translations.literal: Qian Gui's younger clan brother Ke Tan came to flee; Guang issued a document saying, "Qian Gui has a wolf cub's wild heart; front and back he reverses and repeats.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke Tan, a cousin of Qian Gui, defected, Lü Guang issued an edict: "Qian Gui is a wolf cub at heart and has turned traitor again and again.

sentences.zh: 朕方東清秦、趙，勒銘會稽，豈令豎子鴟峙洮南！

translations.literal: I am about to east clear Qin and Zhao, carve an inscription at Kuaiji; how could I allow a brat to owl-perch south of the Tao!
translations.idiomatic: I mean to pacify Qin and Zhao in the east and carve my victory stele at Kuaiji. I will not let some boy squat like an owl south of the Tao!

sentences.zh: 且其兄弟內相離間，可乘之機，勿過今也。

translations.literal: Moreover his brothers internally mutually estrange one another; the opportunity that can be exploited must not pass today.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers are tearing one another apart within the clan; the moment must be seized now.

sentences.zh: 其敕中外戒嚴，朕當親討。

translations.literal: Order central and external martial vigilance; I shall personally punish.
translations.idiomatic: Order full mobilization within and without; I shall lead the punitive expedition myself.

sentences.zh: 」光於是次於長最，使呂纂率楊軌、竇苟等步騎三萬攻金城。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon halted at Changzui and sent Lü Zuan to lead Yang Gui, Dou Gou, and others with thirty thousand foot and horse to attack Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Changzui and sent Lü Zuan with Yang Gui, Dou Gou, and thirty thousand infantry and cavalry against Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 乾歸率眾二萬救之。

translations.literal: Qian Gui led twenty thousand troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gui marched twenty thousand men to its relief.

sentences.zh: 光遣其將王寶、徐炅率騎五千邀之，乾歸懼而不進。

translations.literal: Guang sent his generals Wang Bao and Xu Jiong to lead five thousand horse to intercept him; Qian Gui feared and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Wang Bao and Xu Jiong with five thousand horsemen blocked his path, and Qian Gui hesitated to advance.

sentences.zh: 光又遣其將梁恭、金石生以甲卒萬餘出陽武下峽，與秦州刺史沒奕于攻其東，光弟天水公延以枹罕之眾攻臨洮、武始、河關，皆克之。

translations.literal: Guang again sent his generals Liang Gong and Jin Shisheng with more than ten thousand armored soldiers out of Yangwu down the gorge, together with Qinzhou Provincial Governor Moyeyu to attack his east; Guang's younger brother the Duke of Tianshui Yan with the Fuhan crowds attacked Lintao, Wushi, and Heguan, and all were overcome.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Liang Gong and Jin Shisheng with more than ten thousand armored troops through the Yangwu defile to join Governor Moyeyu of Qin province in striking the eastern front, while his brother Yan the Duke of Tianshui advanced from Fuhan against Lintao, Wushi, and Heguan, all of which fell.

sentences.zh: 呂纂克金城，擒乾歸金城太守衛犍，犍瞋目謂光曰：「我寧守節斷頭，不為降虜也。

translations.literal: Lü Zuan took Jincheng and captured Qian Gui's Jincheng prefect Wei Jian; Jian glared with his eyes and said to Guang, "I would rather keep integrity and have my head cut than be a surrendering barbarian."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan seized Jincheng and took the prefect Wei Jian alive. Glaring at Lü Guang, Wei Jian said, "I would sooner die keeping my honor than live as your captive."

sentences.zh: 」光義而免之。

translations.literal: Guang deemed him righteous and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang admired his spirit and spared him.

sentences.zh: 乾歸因大震，泣歎曰：「死中求生，正在今日也。

translations.literal: Qian Gui therefore was greatly shaken, wept and sighed, saying, "Seeking life within death is just today."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gui was shaken and wept, "To wrest life from death—today is the day.

sentences.zh: 」乃縱反間，稱乾歸眾潰，東奔成紀。

translations.literal: Then he spread counter-espionage, claiming Qian Gui's host had routed and fled east to Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: He sowed deception that his army had broken and fled east toward Chengji.

sentences.zh: 呂延信之，引師輕進。

translations.literal: Lü Yan believed it and led the army lightly forward.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yan believed the rumor and pushed ahead recklessly.

sentences.zh: 延司馬耿稚諫曰：「乾歸雄勇過人，權略難測，破王廣，克楊定，皆羸師以誘之，雖蕞爾小國，亦不可輕也。

translations.literal: Yan's Major Geng Zhi admonished, saying, "Qian Gui's heroism and bravery surpass others; stratagem and plan are hard to fathom; he defeated Wang Guang and overcame Yang Ding, all with weak troops to entice them; although a trivial small state, it also cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: His major Geng Zhi warned him: "Qian Gui surpasses other men in valor and cunning. He broke Wang Guang and destroyed Yang Ding by baiting them with feigned weakness. Even a small state must not be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 困獸猶鬥，況乾歸而可望風自散乎！

translations.literal: A cornered beast still fights; how much more Qian Gui, and can one expect him to scatter of himself at the wind!
translations.idiomatic: A cornered beast will still fight—how can we expect Qian Gui's host to melt away at rumor?

sentences.zh: 且告者視高而色動，必為奸計。

translations.literal: Moreover the informer's look was high and his color moved; it must be a treacherous plan.
translations.idiomatic: The scouts looked smug and nervous; it must be a ruse.

sentences.zh: 而今宜部陣而前，步騎相接，徐待諸軍大集，可一舉滅之。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to deploy lines forward, foot and horse mutually connect, slowly wait until the various armies greatly gather, and then one stroke can extinguish him.
translations.idiomatic: We should advance in ordered ranks, keep infantry and cavalry linked, wait until our full force assembles, and then destroy him at a blow.

sentences.zh: 」延不從，與乾歸相遇，戰敗，死之。

translations.literal: Yan did not follow; he met Qian Gui, was defeated in battle, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused, met Qian Gui in battle, was routed, and died.

sentences.zh: 耿稚及將軍姜顯收集散卒，屯於枹罕。

translations.literal: Geng Zhi and General Jiang Xian gathered scattered soldiers and encamped at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zhi and General Jiang Xian rallied the broken units and held Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 光還于姑臧。

translations.literal: Guang returned to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang withdrew to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 光荒耄信讒，殺尚書沮渠羅仇、三河太守沮渠麹粥。

translations.literal: Guang was senile and believed slander; he killed Minister Juqu Luochou and Sanhe prefect Juqu Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Age and credulity led Lü Guang to heed slander; he executed Minister Juqu Luochou and Juqu Quzhou, prefect of Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 羅仇弟子蒙遜叛光，殺中田護軍馬邃，攻陷臨松郡，屯兵金山，大為百姓之患。

translations.literal: Luochou's disciple nephew Mengxun rebelled against Guang, killed Central Field Protector Ma Sui, attacked and took Linsong commandery, stationed troops on Jin Mountain, and greatly became a calamity for the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Luochou's nephew Mengxun broke away, killed Protector of the Armies Ma Sui, overran Linsong commandery, and encamped on Mount Jin, becoming a scourge to the people.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜從兄男成先為將軍，守晉昌，聞蒙遜起兵，逃奔貲虜，扇動諸夷，眾至數千，進攻福祿、建安。

translations.literal: Mengxun's elder male cousin Nancheng first was a general guarding Jinchang; hearing Mengxun raised troops, he fled to Zilu, fanned and moved the various Yi, the crowd reached several thousand, and advanced to attack Fulu and Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin Nancheng had been a general holding Jinchang; hearing of Mengxun's uprising he fled to Zilu, stirred the tribes, gathered several thousand men, and struck toward Fulu and Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 甯戎護軍趙策擊敗之，男成退屯樂涫。

translations.literal: Ningrong Protector Zhao Ce defeated him; Nancheng retreated and encamped at Legu.
translations.idiomatic: Protector of Ningrong Zhao Ce beat him back, and Nancheng withdrew to Legu.

sentences.zh: 呂纂敗蒙遜于忽穀。

translations.literal: Lü Zuan defeated Mengxun at Hugu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan defeated Mengxun in the Hugu valley.

sentences.zh: 酒泉太守壘澄率將軍趙策、趙陵步騎萬餘討男成于樂涫，戰敗，澄、策死之。

translations.literal: Jiuquan prefect Lei Cheng led generals Zhao Ce and Zhao Ling with more than ten thousand foot and horse to punish Nancheng at Legu; they were defeated in battle, and Cheng and Ce died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Cheng, governor of Jiuquan, led generals Zhao Ce and Zhao Ling with more than ten thousand men against Nancheng at Legu but lost; Lei Cheng and Zhao Ce died in the fight.

sentences.zh: 男成進攻建康，說太守段業曰：「呂氏政衰，權臣擅命，刑罰失中，人不堪役，一州之地，叛者連城，瓦解之勢，昭然在目，百姓嗷然，無所宗附。

translations.literal: Nancheng advanced to attack Jiankang and persuaded prefect Duan Ye, saying, "The Lü clan's governance declines; powerful ministers monopolize command; punishments lose the mean; people cannot bear corvée; in one province's territory rebels connect cities; the trend of disintegration is clear in the eyes; the hundred surnames clamor and have nowhere to attach.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng pressed the attack on Jiankang and urged Prefect Duan Ye: "The Lü house is failing, strongmen seize orders, punishments are unjust, and the people cannot endure labor service. Whole districts rise across the province; the collapse is plain, the commoners cry out with no leader to follow.

sentences.zh: 府君豈可以蓋世之才，而立忠於垂亡之世！

translations.literal: Sir, how can you with world-covering talent yet stand loyal to an age about to perish!
translations.idiomatic: With your rare abilities will you cling to loyalty in a realm about to perish?

sentences.zh: 男成等既唱大義，欲屈府君撫臨鄙州，使塗炭之余蒙來蘇之惠。

translations.literal: Nancheng and others, having proclaimed the great cause, wish to persuade you, Prefect, to come and oversee our humble province, so that those who survive utter ruin may receive the blessing of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: We have raised the banner of righteousness and ask you, Prefect, to take charge of our commandery so that a people laid waste may know deliverance.

sentences.zh: 」業不從。

translations.literal: Ye did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye refused.

sentences.zh: 相持二旬而外救不至，郡人高逵、史惠等言於業曰：「今孤城獨立，台無救援，府君雖心過田單，而地非即墨，宜思高算，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: They faced each other twenty days but no relief came from outside; the commandery men Gao Kui, Shi Hui, and others said to Ye, "Now this lone city stands isolated and no aid comes from the court. Though your resolve may rival Tian Dan's, this ground is not Jimo; you should weigh a higher plan and turn peril into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days of stalemate with no reinforcements, Gao Kui, Shi Hui, and others urged Duan Ye: "The city stands alone and the throne sends no help. Your spirit may match Tian Dan's, but you are not at Jimo. You need a bold strategy to turn disaster into opportunity.

sentences.zh: 」業先與光侍中房晷、僕射王詳不平，慮不自容，乃許之。

translations.literal: Ye had long been at odds with Guang's Palace Attendant Fang Jiu and Vice Director Wang Xiang and feared he could not remain; then he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye had already quarreled with Fang Jiu and Wang Xiang at Lü Guang's court and doubted he could stay safe, so he accepted.

sentences.zh: 男成等推業為大都督、龍驤大將軍、涼州牧、建康公。

translations.literal: Nancheng and others raised Ye as Grand Area Commander, Dragon-Prancing Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng and his party proclaimed Duan Ye grand commander, Dragon-Prancing Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 光命呂纂討業，沮渠蒙遜進屯臨洮，為業聲勢。

translations.literal: Guang ordered Lü Zuan to campaign against Ye; Juqu Mengxun advanced and encamped at Lintao to bolster Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent Lü Zuan against Duan Ye while Juqu Mengxun moved to Lintao to support him.

sentences.zh: 戰于合離，纂師大敗。

translations.literal: They fought at Heli; Zuan's army was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Heli, Lü Zuan's force suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 光散騎常侍、太常郭黁明天文，善占候，謂王詳曰：「于天文，涼之分野將有大兵。

translations.literal: Guang's Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Ceremonies Guo Nen understood astronomy and was skilled at reading omens; he said to Wang Xiang, "By the stars, Liang's allotted region will see great war.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen, Lü Guang's cavalier attendant and minister of rites, was expert at the heavens and divination. He told Wang Xiang, "The astral field for Liang foretells major warfare.

sentences.zh: 主上老病，太子沖暗，纂等凶武，一旦不諱，必有難作。

translations.literal: The ruler is old and ill; the crown prince is young and dull; Zuan and the rest are fierce in arms; once he dies, trouble is sure to break out.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is aged and ailing, the heir is young and dim, and Lü Zuan and his ilk are violent soldiers. When the old man passes, crisis will follow.

sentences.zh: 以吾二人久居內要，常有不善之言，恐禍及人，深宜慮之。

translations.literal: Because we two have long held sensitive posts inside, ill words are often spoken; I fear disaster will reach others; you should think deeply on this.
translations.idiomatic: We have long held inner power, and people speak ill of us. Calamity may reach us both unless we plan carefully.

sentences.zh: 田胡王氣乞機部眾最強，二苑之人多其故眾。

translations.literal: Among the Tianhu, Wang Qiji's following was the strongest; many people in the two palace parks were his old adherents.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Tianhu tribesmen, Wang Qiji commanded the strongest band, and the two royal parks teemed with his former followers.

sentences.zh: 吾今與公唱義，推機為主，則二苑之眾盡我有也。

translations.literal: I now with you will proclaim the cause and raise Ji as leader; then the crowds of the two parks will all be ours.
translations.idiomatic: If you and I proclaim a righteous rising and set Qiji at the head, we can win over everyone in both parks.

sentences.zh: 克城之後，徐更圖之。

translations.literal: After the city is taken, we may plan further at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold the capital, we can decide the next move in our own time.

sentences.zh: 」詳以為然。

translations.literal: Xiang deemed it right.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang agreed.

sentences.zh: 夜燒光洪範門，二苑之眾皆附之，詳為內應。

translations.literal: At night they burned Guang's Hongfan Gate; the crowds of the two parks all joined them; Xiang was the inside accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: They torched the Hongfan Gate by night, the two parks rose with them, and Wang Xiang acted as their agent inside.

sentences.zh: 事發，光誅之。

translations.literal: When the plot was exposed, Guang executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The conspiracy surfaced and Lü Guang put them to death.

sentences.zh: 黁遂據東苑以叛。

translations.literal: Nen then seized the east park and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen then occupied the eastern park and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 光馳使召纂，諸將勸纂曰：「業聞師回，必躡軍後。

translations.literal: Guang sent a swift messenger to recall Zuan; the generals urged Zuan, "If Ye learns the army is turning back, he will surely trail us and strike the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang urgently recalled Lü Zuan. His officers warned him, "Duan Ye will shadow our retreat and hit us from behind if he hears we are coming home.

sentences.zh: 若潛師夜還，庶無後患矣。

translations.literal: If we steal a march by night, perhaps there will be no later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: A silent night march is our best hope of avoiding that.

sentences.zh: 」纂曰：「業雖憑城阻眾，無雄略之才，若夜潛還，張其奸志。

translations.literal: Zuan said, "Although Ye relies on his walls and numbers, he lacks bold strategy; if we slip away by night, we only feed his treacherous ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan replied, "Duan Ye is no strategist despite his walls and men. Sneaking home would only embolden him.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使告業曰：「郭黁作亂，吾今還都。

translations.literal: Then he sent a messenger to tell Ye, "Guo Nen has risen; I am returning to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Duan Ye: "Guo Nen has mutinied; I am marching back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卿能決者，可出戰。

translations.literal: If you dare decide, come out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to contest this, meet me in the field.

sentences.zh: 」於是引還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his host.

sentences.zh: 業不敢出。

translations.literal: Ye dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye stayed behind his walls.

sentences.zh: 纂司馬楊統謂其從兄恆曰：「郭黁明善天文，起兵其當有以。

translations.literal: Zuan's Major Yang Tong said to his cousin Heng, "Guo Nen is skilled at reading the heavens; his revolt must rest on some omen.
translations.idiomatic: Major Yang Tong told his cousin Heng, "Guo Nen reads the stars; he would not rise without a sign.

sentences.zh: 京城之外非復朝廷之有，纂今還都，復何所補！

translations.literal: Beyond the capital is no longer the court's to command; Zuan now returns to the capital—what good does that do!
translations.idiomatic: The capital's outskirts are already lost to the throne. What does Lü Zuan's homecoming change?

sentences.zh: 統請除纂，勒兵推兄為盟主，西襲呂弘，據張掖以號令諸郡，亦千載一時也。

translations.literal: Tong asks to remove Zuan, take the troops, and raise you, elder brother, as covenant lord; strike west at Lü Hong, hold Zhangye, and command the commanderies—it is the chance of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Let us kill Lü Zuan, put you at the head of the host, strike west against Lü Hong, seize Zhangye, and call the provinces to obey—the opportunity of a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 」桓怒曰：「吾聞臣子之事君親，有隕無二，吾未有包胥存救之效，豈可安榮其祿，亂增其難乎！

translations.literal: Huan angrily said, "I have heard that serving lord and parent allows no divided loyalty; I have not wrought a rescue like Shen Baoxu's—how could I cling to salary and add to their peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan flared, "A subject owes his prince undivided duty. I am no Shen Baoxu saving a fallen state. I will not fatten myself on office and deepen the realm's woes!"

sentences.zh: 呂宗若敗，吾為弘演矣。

translations.literal: If the house of Lü falls, I shall be another Hong Yan.
translations.idiomatic: If the Lü clan collapses, I shall play Hong Yan to the end.

sentences.zh: 」統懼，至番禾，遂奔郭黁。

translations.literal: Tong feared; reaching Fanhe, he fled to Guo Nen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong took fright, reached Fanhe, and defected to Guo Nen.

sentences.zh: 黁遣軍邀纂于白石，纂大敗。

translations.literal: Nen sent troops to intercept Zuan at Baishi; Zuan was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen's force ambushed Lü Zuan at Baishi and routed him.

sentences.zh: 光西安太守石元良率步騎五千赴難，與纂共擊黁軍，破之，遂入于姑臧。

translations.literal: Guang's Xi'an prefect Shi Yuanliang led five thousand foot and horse to the rescue; together with Zuan he struck Nen's army, defeated it, and entered Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yuanliang, prefect of Xi'an under Lü Guang, brought five thousand men to the relief; he and Lü Zuan broke Guo Nen's line and fought their way into Guzang.

sentences.zh: 黁之叛也，得光孫八人于東苑。

translations.literal: When Nen rebelled, he had taken eight of Guang's grandsons in the east park.
translations.idiomatic: At the outbreak of Guo Nen's revolt he had seized eight of Lü Guang's grandsons in the eastern park.

sentences.zh: 及軍敗，恚甚，悉投之於鋒刃之上，枝分節解，飲血盟眾，眾皆掩目，不忍視之，黁悠然自若。

translations.literal: When his army lost, he was furious; he threw them all onto blades, hacked them limb from limb, drank blood and swore the crowd; the crowd covered their eyes and could not bear to look; Nen was calm and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat he flew into a rage, impaled the boys on weapons, carved them apart, and swore his men in their blood while they hid their eyes; Guo Nen alone looked on unmoved.

sentences.zh: 黁推後將軍楊軌為盟主，軌自稱大將軍、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: Nen raised Rear General Yang Gui as covenant lord; Gui styled himself Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen made Rear General Yang Gui his war chief; Yang Gui proclaimed himself Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 呂纂擊黁將王斐於城西，大破之，自是黁勢漸衰。

translations.literal: Lü Zuan struck Nen's general Wang Fei west of the city and heavily defeated him; from this Nen's power gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan crushed Guo Nen's officer Wang Fei west of the walls, and Guo Nen's strength ebbed thereafter.

sentences.zh: 光遺楊軌書曰：「自羌胡不靖，郭黁叛逆，南籓安否，音問兩絕。

translations.literal: Guang sent Yang Gui a letter saying, "Since Qiang and Hu unrest and Guo Nen's rebellion, I have had no word whether the southern frontier is safe.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang wrote to Yang Gui: "Trouble among Qiang and Hu and Guo Nen's revolt have cut all tidings from the southern marches.

sentences.zh: 行人風傳，雲卿擁逼百姓，為黁脣齒。

translations.literal: Travelers' rumors say you coerce the commoners and act as Nen's lip and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says you drive the people and stand as Guo Nen's shield and sword.

sentences.zh: 卿雅志忠貞，有史魚之操，鑒察成敗，遠侔古人，豈宜聽納奸邪，以虧大美！

translations.literal: You aspire to loyalty and have Shi Yu's integrity; you judge success and failure and match the ancients—how should you heed treachery and mar your great virtue!
translations.idiomatic: You prize honor like Shi Yu and read fortune like the sages. Do not heed villains and stain your name!

sentences.zh: 陵霜不凋者松柏也，臨難不移者君子也，何圖松柏凋於微霜，雞鳴已於風雨！

translations.literal: What endures frost without withering is pine and cypress; what meets peril without shifting is the gentleman—how could pine and cypress wither at light frost, the cock crow already in wind and rain!
translations.idiomatic: Pine and cypress brave the frost; gentlemen stand firm in peril. Would I see pines fade at a chill or hear the dawn cock in a storm!

sentences.zh: 郭黁巫卜小數，時或誤中，考之大理，率多虛謬。

translations.literal: Guo Nen's sorcery and petty divination sometimes hits by chance; weighed against the great pattern, it is mostly empty error.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen's witchcraft and small tricks may fluke a hit, but in the large design they are hollow lies.

sentences.zh: 朕宰化寡方，澤不逮遠，致世事紛紜，百城離叛。

translations.literal: I rule with scant skill; my grace does not reach far, so the age is tangled and a hundred cities have broken away.
translations.idiomatic: My rule is clumsy and my kindness has not spread; the realm is in chaos and cities rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 戮力一心，同濟巨海者，望之於卿也。

translations.literal: To join strength with one heart and cross the vast sea together—I look to you for that.
translations.idiomatic: I look to you to pull together and sail this great flood as one.

sentences.zh: 今中倉積粟數百千萬，東人戰士一當百餘，入則言笑晏晏，出則武步涼州，吞黁咀業，綽有餘暇。

translations.literal: Now the central granaries hold millions of bushels of grain; eastern fighters match more than a hundred each; at leisure they jest, abroad they stride martially through Liangzhou; swallowing Nen and chewing Ye leaves ample spare force.
translations.idiomatic: Our granaries brim with grain, each eastern soldier is worth a hundred, they rest at ease in camp yet march like wolves abroad, and crushing Guo Nen and Duan Ye would still leave strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 但與卿形雖君臣，心過父子，欲全卿名節，不使貽笑將來。
