translations.literal: Though we are lord and minister in form, my heart toward you is closer than father and son; I wish to preserve your name and integrity and not leave you mocked by posterity.
translations.idiomatic: We are prince and subject in name, yet I favor you as a son; I mean to save your honor from future shame.

sentences.zh: 」軌不答，率步騎二萬北赴郭黁。

translations.literal: Gui did not answer; he led twenty thousand foot and horse north to join Guo Nen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui did not reply; he marched twenty thousand men north to Guo Nen.

sentences.zh: 至姑臧，壘於城北。

translations.literal: Reaching Guzang, he fortified north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Guzang and threw up ramparts north of the walls.

sentences.zh: 軌以士馬之盛，議欲大決成敗，黁每以天文裁之。

translations.literal: Gui, with his host strong, wished to fight a great decisive battle; Nen always checked him with astrology.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui, confident in his numbers, wanted a showdown, but Guo Nen kept him in check with star lore.

sentences.zh: 呂弘為段業所逼，光遣呂纂迎之。

translations.literal: Lü Hong was pressed by Duan Ye; Guang sent Lü Zuan to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye had cornered Lü Hong, so Lü Guang sent Lü Zuan to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 軌謀於眾曰：「呂弘精兵一萬，若與光合，則敵強我弱。

translations.literal: Gui plotted with the assembly, "Lü Hong has ten thousand crack troops; if he joins Guang, the enemy grows strong and we grow weak.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui told his officers, "Lü Hong commands ten thousand veterans. If he joins Lü Guang, we face a stronger foe.

sentences.zh: 養獸不討，將為後患。

translations.literal: To rear a beast and not strike it down will breed later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Spare a beast today and regret it tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」遂率兵邀纂，纂擊敗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops to intercept Zuan; Zuan struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to cut off Lü Zuan, who beat him back.

sentences.zh: 郭黁聞軌敗，東走魏安，遂奔於乞伏乾歸。

translations.literal: Guo Nen heard Gui was defeated, fled east to Weian, then fled to Qifu Qian Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen learned of Yang Gui's defeat, ran east to Weian, and then took refuge with Qifu Qian Gui.

sentences.zh: 楊軌聞黁走，南奔廉川。

translations.literal: Yang Gui heard Nen had fled and ran south to Lianchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui, hearing Guo Nen had gone, bolted south to Lianchuan.

sentences.zh: 光疾甚，立其太子紹為天王，自號太上皇帝。

translations.literal: Guang's illness was severe; he established his crown prince Shao as Heavenly King and styled himself Grand Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang lay gravely ill. He installed Crown Prince Lü Shao as Heavenly King and took the title Grand Supreme Emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 以呂纂為太尉，呂弘為司徒。

translations.literal: He appointed Lü Zuan Grand Commandant and Lü Hong Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lü Zuan grand commandant and Lü Hong minister of education.

sentences.zh: 謂紹曰：「吾疾病唯增，恐將不濟。

translations.literal: He said to Shao, "My sickness only worsens; I fear I will not recover.
translations.idiomatic: He told Lü Shao, "My malady grows worse; I may not survive.

sentences.zh: 三寇窺窬，迭伺國隙。

translations.literal: Three bandits peer and covet, watching in turn for gaps in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Three enemies watch our borders and wait for any crack.

sentences.zh: 吾終以後，使纂統六軍，弘管朝政，汝恭己無為，委重二兄，庶可以濟。

translations.literal: After my end, let Zuan command the six armies and Hong manage court government; you hold yourself in reverent quiet, entrust weight to your two elder brothers, and perhaps the realm can be saved.
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, give Lü Zuan the six armies and Lü Hong the court; keep to modest inaction yourself and lean on your brothers—only so may we endure.

sentences.zh: 若內相猜貳，釁起蕭牆，則晉、趙之變旦夕至矣。

translations.literal: If you suspect each other within and trouble rises inside the screen, then the crises of Jin and Zhao will come overnight.
translations.idiomatic: If kin turn on kin, disaster will arrive as fast as it did for Jin and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 」又謂纂、弘曰：「永業才非撥亂，直以正嫡有常，猥居元首。

translations.literal: Again he said to Zuan and Hong, "Yongye's talent is not for quelling chaos; only because the true heir has a fixed rule does he vulgarly occupy the first seat.
translations.idiomatic: To Lü Zuan and Lü Hong he added, "Yongye cannot master turmoil; he sits as heir only by the rule of primogeniture.

sentences.zh: 今外有強寇，人心未甯，汝兄弟緝穆，則貽厥萬世。

translations.literal: Now outside are strong bandits and hearts are not calm; if you brothers are harmonious, you will bequeath ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Strong foes ring us and the people are uneasy. Brotherly harmony will secure the line for ages.

sentences.zh: 若內自相圖，則禍不旋踵。

translations.literal: If you plot against each other within, calamity will not wait a step.
translations.idiomatic: If you scheme against one another, ruin will come before you turn around.

sentences.zh: 」纂、弘泣曰：「不敢有二心。

translations.literal: Zuan and Hong wept, "We dare not harbor two hearts.
translations.idiomatic: They wept, "We would never harbor disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 」光以安帝隆安三年死，時年六十三，在位十年。

translations.literal: Guang died in Emperor An's third year of Long'an, age sixty-three, having reigned ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang died in the third year of Long'an under Emperor An, at sixty-three, after ten years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 偽諡懿武皇帝，廟號太祖，墓號高陵。

translations.literal: He was falsely posthumously titled Emperor Yiwu, temple name Taizu, tomb name Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: His unauthorized posthumous title was Emperor Yiwu, temple name Taizu, tomb name Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 纂字永緒，光之庶長子也。

translations.literal: Zuan's courtesy name was Yongxu; he was Guang's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan, courtesy name Yongxu, was Lü Guang's eldest son by a concubine.

sentences.zh: 少便弓馬，好鷹犬。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at bow and horse and loved falcons and hounds.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he excelled at riding and archery and doted on hawks and hounds.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時入太學，不好讀書，唯以交結公侯聲樂為務。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian he entered the Imperial Academy; he disliked reading and only busied himself with befriending dukes and marquises and with music.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he attended the Imperial Academy but shunned books, spending his time courting great lords and music.

sentences.zh: 及堅亂，西奔上邽，轉至姑臧，拜武賁中郎將，封太原公。

translations.literal: When Jian's realm collapsed, he fled west to Shanggui, then came to Guzang, was appointed Brave-Gentlemen Household General, and enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian's order fell apart he fled west to Shanggui, then reached Guzang, where he became a Rapid-as-Tigers household general and Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光死，呂紹秘不發喪，纂排閣入哭，盡哀而出。

translations.literal: When Guang died, Lü Shao kept the death secret; Zuan pushed through the gate, entered weeping, and left when his grief was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao hid Lü Guang's death, but Lü Zuan forced the doors, mourned openly, and withdrew when he had spent his grief.

sentences.zh: 紹懼為纂所害，以位讓之，曰：「兄功高年長，宜承大統，願兄勿疑。

translations.literal: Shao feared harm from Zuan and yielded the throne, saying, "Elder brother's merit is high and your years are many; you should inherit the great line; I pray you harbor no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lü Zuan, Lü Shao offered the throne: "Your deeds and age qualify you for the succession; do not doubt my intent.

sentences.zh: 」纂曰：「臣雖年長，陛下國家之塚嫡，不可以私愛而亂大倫。

translations.literal: Zuan said, "Although I am older in years, Your Majesty is the state's legitimate heir; one cannot by private affection disorder the great bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan answered, "I am older, but Your Majesty is the lawful heir; private feeling must not overturn proper order.

sentences.zh: 」紹固以讓纂，纂不許之。

translations.literal: Shao firmly yielded to Zuan; Zuan did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao pressed the offer; Lü Zuan refused.

sentences.zh: 及紹嗣偽位，呂超言於紹曰：「纂統戎積年，威震內外，臨喪不哀，步高視遠，觀其舉止亂常，恐成大變，宜早除之，以安社稷。

translations.literal: When Shao succeeded the false throne, Lü Chao spoke to Shao, "Zuan has commanded arms for years; his awe shakes inside and outside; at mourning he shows no grief; he steps high and looks far; watching his conduct disorder constant, I fear a great change; you should remove him early to secure the altars.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Shao took the unauthorized throne, Lü Chao warned him, "Lü Zuan has led troops for years and inspires fear within and without. He showed no sorrow at the funeral, walks like a conqueror, and acts outside all decency. Strike first or the realm will shake.

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「先帝顧命，音猶在耳，兄弟至親，豈有此乎！

translations.literal: Shao said, "The former lord's testament, its sound still in the ears; brothers are utmost kin—how could there be this!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao replied, "Our father's dying words still ring; we are brothers—how could I?

sentences.zh: 吾弱年而荷大任，方賴二兄以甯家國。

translations.literal: I in weak years bear a great task; I am just relying on the two elder brothers to calm house and state.
translations.idiomatic: I took this heavy burden young and count on my brothers to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 縱其圖我，我視死如歸，終不忍有此意也，卿懼勿過言。

translations.literal: Even if they plot against me, I view death as returning home; in the end I cannot bear this intent; you, fear, do not speak beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they move against me, I accept death rather than plot kin. Do not press me further.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「纂威名素盛，安忍無親，今不圖之，後必噬臍矣。

translations.literal: Chao said, "Zuan's awe name has always been great; he is calm in cruelty and without kin; if we do not plot him now, later we will bite our navels.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao said, "Lü Zuan's name has long inspired terror; he kills without scruple. Ignore him now and we will regret it too late.

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「吾每念袁尚兄弟，未曾不痛心忘寢食，寧坐而死，豈忍行之。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Whenever I think of Yuan Shang's brothers, never do I not pain my heart and forget sleep and food; I would rather sit and die—how could I bear to do it!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao said, "The tale of Yuan Shang's brothers still breaks my heart. I would sooner die in my seat than do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「聖人稱知機其神，陛下臨機不斷，臣見大事去矣。

translations.literal: Chao said, "The sages praise knowing the moment as spirit; Your Majesty at the moment does not decide; I see the great matter is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao answered, "The wise seize the hour. If you hesitate, I see our cause lost.

sentences.zh: 」既而纂見紹於湛露堂，超執刀侍紹，目纂請收之，紹弗許。

translations.literal: Afterward Zuan met Shao at Zhanlu Hall; Chao held a knife attending Shao, signaled Zuan with his eyes asking to seize him; Shao did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Zuan met Lü Shao in the Zhanlu Hall, Lü Chao stood by with a blade and signaled to arrest him, but Lü Shao forbade it.

sentences.zh: 初，光欲立弘為世子，會聞紹在仇池，乃止，弘由是有憾於紹。

translations.literal: Initially Guang had wished to establish Hong as heir; when he heard Shao was in Chouchi, he desisted; Hong from this bore resentment toward Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang had meant to make Lü Hong heir until news of Lü Shao in Chouchi changed his mind, leaving Lü Hong bitter toward Lü Shao.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書姜紀密告纂曰：「先帝登遐，主上暗弱，兄總攝內外，威恩被於遐邇，輒欲遠追廢昌邑之義，以兄為中宗何如？

translations.literal: He sent Minister Jiang Ji secretly to tell Zuan, "The former lord has ascended far; the ruler above is dim and weak; elder brother grasps inside and outside; awe and favor spread near and far; I rashly wish to trace far the principle of deposing the Marquis of Changyi—making elder brother Zhongzong—how would that be?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister Jiang Ji to Lü Zuan in secret: "The late emperor is gone, the young lord is feeble, and you hold power inside and out. Let us follow the precedent of deposing the prince of Changyi and raise you as a new Zhongzong—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」纂於是夜率壯士數百，逾北城，攻廣夏門，弘率東苑之眾斫洪範門。

translations.literal: Zuan thereupon by night led several hundred stalwarts, crossed the north wall, attacked Guangxia Gate; Hong led the east park crowd and hacked the Hongfan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lü Zuan took hundreds of picked men over the north wall against the Guangxia Gate while Lü Hong's eastern park force smashed the Hongfan Gate.

sentences.zh: 左衛齊從守融明觀，逆問之曰：「誰也？

translations.literal: Left Guard Qi Cong guarded Rongming Observatory and met them asking, "Who is it?
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Qi Cong held the Rongming belvedere and challenged them: "Who goes there?

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「太原公。

translations.literal: The crowd said, "The Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 」從曰：「國有大故，主上新立，太原公行不由道，夜入禁城，將為亂邪？

translations.literal: Cong said, "The state has a great mourning; the ruler above is newly raised; the Duke of Taiyuan acts not by the road, enters the forbidden city by night—will there be rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Qi Cong said, "The court is in mourning and a new sovereign sits. The Duke of Taiyuan steals into the palace by night by no proper path—do you mean revolt?

sentences.zh: 」因抽劍直前，斫纂中額。

translations.literal: Therefore he drew his sword straight forward and chopped Zuan in the middle of the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: He drew steel and struck Lü Zuan square on the brow.

sentences.zh: 纂左右擒之，纂曰：「義士也，勿殺。

translations.literal: Zuan's attendants seized him; Zuan said, "He is a righteous man; do not kill.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan's guards seized Qi Cong, but Lü Zuan said, "He is a man of principle; spare him.

sentences.zh: 」紹遣武賁中郎將呂開率其禁兵距戰於端門，驍騎呂超率卒二千赴之。

translations.literal: Shao sent Brave-Gentlemen Household General Lü Kai leading his forbidden troops to resist battle at Duan Gate; crack cavalry Lü Chao led two thousand soldiers to them.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao sent household general Lü Kai with the palace guard to hold the Duan Gate while Lü Chao raced there with two thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 眾素憚纂，悉皆潰散。

translations.literal: The crowd always feared Zuan; all fled scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had always dreaded Lü Zuan and melted away.

sentences.zh: 纂入自青角門，升于謙光殿。

translations.literal: Zuan entered from Qingjiao Gate and ascended Qiangguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan came in through the Qingjiao Gate and mounted the Qiangguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 紹登紫閣自殺，呂超出奔廣武。

translations.literal: Shao ascended the Purple Pavilion and killed himself; Lü Chao fled out to Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao climbed the Purple Pavilion and took his own life; Lü Chao fled to Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 纂憚弘兵強，勸弘即位。

translations.literal: Zuan feared Hong's troops were strong and urged Hong to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan, wary of Lü Hong's army, pressed him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「自以紹弟也而承大統，眾心不順，是以違先帝遺敕，慚負黃泉。

translations.literal: Hong said, "I as Shao's younger brother yet inherited the great line; the crowd's heart was not compliant; therefore I violated the former lord's testament and am ashamed before the Yellow Springs.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong said, "I took the succession as my brother's junior against the people's mind and broke our father's will; I already shame the dead.

sentences.zh: 今復越兄而立，何面目以視息世間！

translations.literal: Now again to leap over the elder brother and establish—what face to draw breath in the world!
translations.idiomatic: To step ahead of my elder brother now—how could I show my face?

sentences.zh: 大兄長且賢，威名振於二賊，宜速即大位，以安國家。

translations.literal: The great elder brother is long in years and worthy; his awe name shakes the two bandits; he should quickly take the great position to calm house and state.
translations.idiomatic: My eldest brother is senior, able, and feared by both enemy houses. He should mount the throne at once to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 」纂以隆安四年遂僭即天王位，大赦境內，改元為咸寧，諡紹為隱王。

translations.literal: Zuan in the fourth year of Long'an then usurped the Heavenly King throne, greatly amnestied within the borders, changed the era to Xianning, and posthumously titled Shao Prince Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Long'an Lü Zuan assumed the Heavenly King title without mandate, ordered a general amnesty, adopted the reign Xianning, and gave Lü Shao the posthumous title Prince Yin.

sentences.zh: 以弘為使持節、侍中、大都督、都督中外諸軍事、大司馬、車騎大將軍、司隸校尉、錄尚書事，改封番禾郡公，其餘封拜各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Hong Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, Palace Attendant, Grand Area Commander, Area Commander of all military affairs of court and field, Grand Marshal, Chariots and Cavalry Grand General, Colonel Director of the Retainers, Recorder of Department of State Affairs, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Fanhe commandery; the rest of enfeoffments and appointments each had grades.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lü Hong Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, palace attendant, grand commander over all military affairs, grand marshal, chariots-and-cavalry general, metropolitan colonel, and recorder of ministerial business, and transferred his fief to Duke of Fanhe; other titles were distributed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 纂謂齊從曰：「卿前斫我，一何甚也！

translations.literal: Zuan said to Qi Cong, "You cut me before—how harsh!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan said to Qi Cong, "That stroke you dealt me was severe!"

sentences.zh: 」從泣曰：「隱王先帝所立，陛下雖應天順時，而微心未達，惟恐陛下不死，何謂甚也。

translations.literal: Cong wept and said, "The Hidden King was established by the former lord; though Your Majesty answers Heaven and follows the season, my humble heart has not understood; I only feared Your Majesty would not die—what do you call harsh?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi Cong wept, "Prince Yin was the late emperor's chosen heir. You hold Heaven's mandate, yet I could not fathom your intent—I only wished you dead. What was excessive in that?"

sentences.zh: 」纂嘉其忠，善遇之。

translations.literal: Zuan praised his loyalty and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan honored his loyalty and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 纂遣使謂征東呂方曰：「超實忠臣，義勇可嘉，但不識經國大體，權變之宜。

translations.literal: Zuan sent a messenger to tell the east-campaigning Lü Fang, "Chao is truly a loyal subject; his righteous bravery is praiseworthy, but he does not grasp the great pattern of governing a state or the fitness of flexible response.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan sent word to Lü Fang on the eastern front: "Lü Chao is loyal and courageous yet ignorant of larger statecraft and expedient policy."

sentences.zh: 方賴其忠節，誕濟世難，可以此意諭之。

translations.literal: We rely on his loyal integrity to carry through the age's crisis; you may explain this meaning to him.
translations.idiomatic: We depend on his constancy to weather this turmoil—make that clear to him.

sentences.zh: 」超上疏陳謝，纂復其爵位。

translations.literal: Chao submitted a memorial stating thanks; Zuan restored his noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao filed a memorial of apology, and Lü Zuan restored his title.

sentences.zh: 呂弘自以功名崇重，恐不為纂所容，纂亦深忌之。

translations.literal: Lü Hong deemed his merit and fame lofty and feared Zuan would not tolerate him; Zuan also deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong thought his achievements too prominent to be safe under Lü Zuan, who in turn deeply mistrusted him.

sentences.zh: 弘遂起兵東苑，劫尹文、楊桓以為謀主，請宗燮俱行。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon raised troops in the east park, seized Yin Wen and Yang Huan to be plot leaders, and asked Zong Xie to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong rose in the eastern park, took Yin Wen and Yang Huan as his strategists, and invited Zong Xie along.

sentences.zh: 燮曰：「老臣受先帝大恩，位為列棘，不能隕身授命，死有餘罪，而復從殿下，親為戎首者，豈天地所容乎！

translations.literal: Xie said, "This old subject received the former lord's great favor and holds a place among the thorn hedges; unable to dash my body and hand over my life, in death there remains guilt; yet to follow Your Highness and personally be chief of arms—how could Heaven and earth contain that!
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xie replied, "The late emperor favored me with high office, yet I failed to die for him—I am guilty enough. To follow you as the first rebel would shame heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 且智不能謀，眾不足恃，將焉用之！

translations.literal: Moreover wisdom cannot plan, numbers are not enough to rely on—where would you use them!
translations.idiomatic: I lack the wit to scheme, and your following is too thin—what use is this rising?

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「君為義士，我為亂臣！

translations.literal: Hong said, "You are a man of principle; I am a traitor!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong shot back, "Then you are the loyalist and I the rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」乃率兵攻纂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops to attack Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against Lü Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纂遣其將焦辨擊弘，弘眾潰，出奔廣武。

translations.literal: Zuan sent his general Jiao Bian to strike Hong; Hong's host broke and he fled to Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan sent Jiao Bian against him; Lü Hong's force collapsed and he bolted to Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 纂縱兵大掠，以東苑婦女賞軍，弘之妻子亦為士卒所辱。

translations.literal: Zuan let his troops plunder greatly, gave the east park women as rewards to the army, and Hong's wife and children were also humiliated by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan unleashed a general looting, handed out women from the eastern park as spoils, and Lü Hong's family was abused by the troops.

sentences.zh: 纂笑謂群臣曰：「今日之戰何如？

translations.literal: Zuan smiled and said to the host of officials, "How was today's battle?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan asked his court with a smile, "What did you make of today's fight?"

sentences.zh: 」其侍中房晷對曰：「天禍涼室，釁起戚籓。

translations.literal: His Palace Attendant Fang Jiu replied, "Heaven sends calamity on the house of Liang; trouble rises within the kin screens.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jiu answered, "Heaven scourges Liang: kin turn blades on kin."

sentences.zh: 先帝始崩，隱王幽逼，山陵甫訖，大司馬驚疑肆逆，京邑交兵，友于接刃。

translations.literal: The former lord had just died; the Hidden King was cornered; the mausoleum had barely finished when the Grand Marshal, startled and suspicious, wantonly rebelled; the capital crossed arms; brothers of friendship met blades.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had the late emperor fallen than Prince Yin was trapped. The tomb was still fresh when the grand marshal turned traitor, the capital erupted in fighting, and brothers crossed swords.

sentences.zh: 雖弘自取夷滅，亦由陛下無棠棣之義。

translations.literal: Although Hong brought ruin on himself, it is also because Your Majesty lacked the meaning of the pear-tree brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong courted his own doom, yet you too showed none of the brotherly love the Tang pear trees symbolize.

sentences.zh: 宜考已責躬，以謝百姓，而反縱兵大掠，幽辱士女。

translations.literal: You should examine yourself and blame your person to apologize to the hundred surnames; instead you let troops plunder greatly and humiliate gentlemen and women.
translations.idiomatic: You should humble yourself before the people, yet you sanctioned rape and pillage against gentry and women.

sentences.zh: 釁自由弘，百姓何罪！

translations.literal: The fault began with Hong—what crime have the hundred surnames!
translations.idiomatic: The guilt is Lü Hong's—what did commoners do to deserve this?

sentences.zh: 且弘妻，陛下之弟婦也；

translations.literal: Moreover Hong's wife is Your Majesty's younger brother's wife;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lü Hong's wife is your sister-in-law;

sentences.zh: 弘女，陛下之侄女也。

translations.literal: Hong's daughter is Your Majesty's niece.
translations.idiomatic: his daughter is your niece.

sentences.zh: 奈何使無賴小人辱為婢妾。

translations.literal: How could you let worthless men dishonor them as concubine-slaves.
translations.idiomatic: How could you let rabble degrade them as concubines?

sentences.zh: 天地神明，豈忍見此！

translations.literal: Heaven, earth, and the spirits—could they bear to see this!
translations.idiomatic: Would heaven and earth look on such cruelty without flinching!

sentences.zh: 」遂歔欷悲泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sobbed and wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down weeping.

sentences.zh: 纂改容謝之，召弘妻及男女于東宮，厚撫之。

translations.literal: Zuan changed countenance and apologized to him; he summoned Hong's wife and children and sons and daughters to the eastern palace and treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan softened, apologized, and brought Lü Hong's family to the eastern palace with rich consolation.

sentences.zh: 呂方執弘系獄，馳使告纂，纂遣力士康龍拉殺之。

translations.literal: Lü Fang seized Hong, bound him in prison, sent a swift messenger to report to Zuan, and Zuan sent strongman Kang Long to drag and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fang captured Lü Hong, jailed him, and reported to Lü Zuan, who sent Kang Long to haul him out and strangle him.

sentences.zh: 是月，立其妻楊氏為皇后，以楊氏父桓為散騎常侍、尚書左僕射、涼都尹，封金城侯。

translations.literal: That month he established his wife Lady Yang as empress, appointed Lady Yang's father Huan as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Vice Director of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, Intendant of the Liang capital, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The same month he made Lady Yang empress, named her father Yang Huan cavalier attendant, left vice director of state affairs, intendant of the Liang capital, and Marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 纂將伐禿髮利鹿孤，中書令楊穎諫曰：「夫起師動眾，必參之天人，苟非其時，聖賢所不為。

translations.literal: Zuan was about to campaign against Tufa Lilugu; Director of the Secretariat Yang Ying remonstrated, "Raising armies and moving hosts must be referred to Heaven and man; if it is not the time, sages do not do it.
translations.idiomatic: As Lü Zuan prepared war on Tufa Lilugu, Yang Ying warned, "War demands the right moment in heaven and on earth; sages refuse ill-timed campaigns."

sentences.zh: 禿髮利鹿孤上下用命，國未有釁，不可以伐。

translations.literal: Tufa Lilugu above and below obey commands; the state has no crack; one cannot attack.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu's realm obeys him and shows no crack—this is no time to strike.

sentences.zh: 宜繕甲養銳，勸課農殖，待可乘之機，然後一舉蕩滅。

translations.literal: It is fitting to repair armor, nurture sharpness, encourage farming, wait for an opportunity that can be exploited, then in one stroke sweep them away.
translations.idiomatic: Repair arms, rest the army, push farming, and move only when a gap opens—then wipe them out at one blow.

sentences.zh: 比年多事，公私罄竭，不深根固本，恐為患將來，願抑赫斯之怒，思萬全之算。

translations.literal: Year after year there have been many affairs; public and private are drained; if we do not deepen roots and firm the base, I fear trouble in the future; I wish you would restrain imperial wrath and ponder a plan of perfect safety.
translations.idiomatic: Years of strife have emptied the treasury and the people. Without rebuilding strength you court future peril—check your anger and choose the sure path.

sentences.zh: 」纂不從。

translations.literal: Zuan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 度浩亹河，為鹿弧弟傉檀所敗，遂西襲張掖。

translations.literal: He crossed the Haomen River and was defeated by Lilugu's younger brother Nutan; then he struck west at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Haomen River but Tufa Rutan, Lilugu's brother, routed him, so he veered west against Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 姜紀諫曰：「方今盛夏，百姓廢農，所利既少，所喪者多，若師至嶺西，虜必乘虛寇抄都下，宜且回師以為後圖。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji remonstrated, "It is high summer; the hundred surnames abandon farming; what is gained is little and what is lost is much; if the army reaches west of the ranges, the barbarians will surely seize the void to raid the capital below—it is fitting to turn the army back for later planning.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji urged him, "Midsummer idles the farmers for little gain. If we push past the mountains, the foe will raid an empty capital—withdraw and plan again."

sentences.zh: 」纂曰：「虜無大志，聞朕西征，正可自固耳。

translations.literal: Zuan said, "The barbarians have no great ambition; hearing that I march west, they can only shore themselves up.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan answered, "They lack grand designs; news of our western march will only make them dig in."

sentences.zh: 今速襲之，可以得志。

translations.literal: Now if we strike them swiftly, we can achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: A quick blow now can still succeed.

sentences.zh: 」遂圍張掖，略地建康。

translations.literal: Thereupon he besieged Zhangye and raided the land of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Zhangye and swept the Jiankang district.

sentences.zh: 聞傉檀寇姑臧，乃還。

translations.literal: Hearing that Nutan was raiding Guzang, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Tufa Rutan was striking Guzang, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 即序胡安據盜發張駿墓，見駿貌如生，得真珠簏、琉璃榼、白玉樽、赤玉簫、紫玉笛、珊瑚鞭、馬腦鐘，水陸奇珍不可勝紀。

translations.literal: A Jixu Hu named An Ju robbed open Zhang Jun's tomb; he saw Jun's appearance as if alive and obtained a pearl casket, glass ewer, white jade goblet, red jade panpipe, purple jade flute, coral whip, agate bell, and land and water rarities beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: An Ju of the Jixu Hu broke into Zhang Jun's tomb and found the corpse as if alive, hauling off pearl boxes, glass vessels, jade cups and pipes, a coral whip, an agate bell, and treasures without number.

sentences.zh: 纂誅安據党五十餘家，遣使弔祭駿，並繕修其墓。

translations.literal: Zuan executed An Ju's faction of more than fifty households, sent envoys to condole and sacrifice to Jun, and also repaired his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan wiped out An Ju's fifty-odd allied families, sent officials to mourn Zhang Jun, and restored the tomb.

sentences.zh: 道士句摩羅耆婆言於纂曰：「潛龍屢出，豕犬見妖，將有下人謀上之禍，宜增修德政，以答天戒。

translations.literal: The Daoist Goumolu Qipo said to Zuan, "The hidden dragon has repeatedly emerged; pigs and dogs show prodigies; there will be disaster of inferiors plotting superiors; it is fitting to increase and cultivate virtuous government to answer Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Kumarajiva warned Lü Zuan, "Omens speak of a hidden dragon and beast signs—vassals may strike their lord. Answer heaven with better rule."

sentences.zh: 」纂納之。

translations.literal: Zuan accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan took the advice.

sentences.zh: 耆婆，即羅什之別名也。

translations.literal: Qipo was another name for Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: That teacher was another name for Kumarajiva.

sentences.zh: 纂游田無度，荒耽酒色，其太常楊穎諫曰：「臣聞皇天降鑒，惟德是與。

translations.literal: Zuan hunted and toured without limit, wastefully addicted to wine and women; his Minister of Ceremonies Yang Ying remonstrated, "Your subject has heard that August Heaven mirrors down and grants only to virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan hunted without restraint and drowned in wine and women. Yang Ying said, "High heaven favors only those who show virtue."

sentences.zh: 德由人弘，天應以福，故勃焉之美奄在聖躬。

translations.literal: Virtue is enlarged by men; Heaven responds with blessing; therefore the beauty of sudden rise rests in the sage's person.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue draws heaven's blessing; your sudden rise owed to that power.

sentences.zh: 大業已爾，宜以道守之。

translations.literal: The great enterprise is already thus; it is fitting to guard it with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you hold the throne, you must guard it with right conduct.

sentences.zh: 廓靈基於日新，邀洪福于萬祀。

translations.literal: Broaden the numinous foundation through daily renewal; invite vast blessing through myriad sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Renew your mandate day by day and seek lasting fortune for the altars.

sentences.zh: 自陛下龍飛，疆宇未辟，崎嶇二嶺之內，綱維未振於九州。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's dragon flight, the borderlands are not yet opened; within the crooked two ranges the net-cords have not yet been raised over the nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Since you took the throne the realm beyond the passes is unconquered and order does not yet span the nine provinces.

sentences.zh: 當兢兢夕惕，經略四方，成先帝之遺志，拯蒼生於荼蓼。

translations.literal: You ought to tremble with evening caution, plan strategy on four sides, complete the former lord's unfulfilled intent, and save the black-haired folk from bitter hardship.
translations.idiomatic: You should live in vigilant fear, campaign to finish your father's work, and lift the people from misery.

sentences.zh: 而更飲酒過度，出入無恆，宴安游盤之樂，沈湎樽酒之間，不以寇仇為慮，竊為陛下危之。

translations.literal: Yet you further drink wine excessively, go in and out without constancy, take pleasure in feasting and roaming, sink and drown between goblet and wine, do not take enemy and foe as concern—I privately fear for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you drink without measure, come and go at whim, revel in hunts and feasts, and ignore your enemies—I tremble for you, Sire.

sentences.zh: 糟丘酒池，洛汭不返，皆陛下之殷鑒。

translations.literal: Wine pools and dregs hills, the Luo ford and no return—all are bright mirrors for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The wine pools of Zhou and the drowned kings of old are warnings carved for you.

sentences.zh: 臣蒙先帝夷險之恩，故不敢避幹將之戮。

translations.literal: Your subject received the former lord's favor through peril and peace; therefore I dare not avoid the executioner's blade.
translations.idiomatic: Your father favored me through thick and thin; I speak though it cost my neck.

sentences.zh: 」纂曰：「朕之罪也。

translations.literal: Zuan said, "It is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan said, "The fault is mine."

sentences.zh: 不有貞亮之士，誰匡邪僻之君！

translations.literal: If there were no upright and bright gentlemen, who would correct a depraved lord!
translations.idiomatic: Without honest ministers, who would set a wayward ruler straight?

sentences.zh: 」然昏虐自任，終不能改，常與左右因醉馳獵於坑澗之間，殿中侍御史王回、中書侍郎王儒扣馬諫曰：「千金之子坐不垂堂，萬乘之主清道而行，奈何去輿輦之安，冒奔騎之危！

translations.literal: Yet he was benighted and cruel on his own and in the end could not reform; he constantly with his attendants, because of drunkenness, galloped and hunted in the gullies; Palace Attendant Censor Wang Hui and Secretariat Gentleman Wang Ru seized the reins and remonstrated, "The child of a thousand in gold does not sit beneath a sagging eave; the lord of ten thousand chariots clears the road and goes—how can you leave the safety of carriage and palanquin and brave the peril of bolting steeds!
translations.idiomatic: He never mended his ways. Drunk, he raced through ravines with his favorites until Wang Hui and Wang Ru seized his reins: "A noble heir avoids crumbling eaves; a Son of Heaven travels with roads cleared—why trade your palanquin for a reckless ride!"

sentences.zh: 銜橛之變，動有不測之禍。

translations.literal: A mishap of bit or bar brings unforeseen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: A slipped rein can kill you before you know it.

sentences.zh: 愚臣竊所不安，敢以死爭，願陛下遠思袁盎攬轡之言，不令臣等受譏千載。

translations.literal: This foolish subject privately is uneasy; I dare contend with death; I wish Your Majesty would think far on Yuan Ang's words about seizing the reins, and not let your subjects be mocked for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I risk death to say it: remember Yuan Ang's warning about the reins—do not make us a laughingstock for ages.

sentences.zh: 」纂不納。

translations.literal: Zuan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan ignored them.

sentences.zh: 纂番禾太守呂超擅伐鮮卑思盤，思盤遣弟乞珍訴超於纂，纂召超將盤入朝。

translations.literal: Zuan's Fanhe prefect Lü Chao on his own authority attacked the Xianbei Sipan; Sipan sent his younger brother Qizhen to accuse Chao to Zuan, and Zuan summoned Chao to bring Sipan to court.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao, governor of Fanhe, raided the Xianbei chief Sipan without orders. Sipan sent Qizhen to complain, and Lü Zuan ordered Chao to escort Sipan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 超至姑臧，大懼，自結於殿中監杜尚，纂見超，怒曰：「卿恃兄弟桓桓，欲欺吾也，要當斬卿，然後天下可定。

translations.literal: When Chao reached Guzang, he was greatly afraid and attached himself to Palace Inspector Du Shang; Zuan saw Chao and angrily said, "You rely on your brothers' martial bearing and wish to deceive me; I must behead you, then the realm can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao reached Guzang in terror and bribed Du Shang. Lü Zuan snarled, "You trust your brothers' brawn to mock me—I should take your head before the realm is steady."

sentences.zh: 」超頓首不敢。

translations.literal: Chao knocked his head and dared not.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao kowtowed and stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 纂因引超及其諸臣宴於內殿。

translations.literal: Zuan thereupon led Chao and his various ministers to feast in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan then feasted Lü Chao and the ministers in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 呂隆屢勸纂酒，已至昏醉，乘步輓車將超等游於內。

translations.literal: Lü Long repeatedly urged Zuan to drink until he was muddily drunk; riding a hand-drawn cart he took Chao and the others touring inside.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long kept pouring wine until Lü Zuan was blind drunk, then toured the inner grounds with him and Lü Chao in a handcart.

sentences.zh: 至琨華堂東閤，車不得過，纂親將竇川、駱騰倚劍於壁，推車過閤。

translations.literal: Reaching the east wing of Kunhua Hall, the cart could not pass; Zuan's personal generals Dou Chuan and Luo Teng leaned swords on the wall and pushed the cart through the wing.
translations.idiomatic: At Kunhua Hall's east wing the cart stuck; Dou Chuan and Luo Teng propped swords against the wall and shoved it through.

sentences.zh: 超取劍擊纂，纂下車擒超，超刺纂洞胸，奔於宣德堂。

translations.literal: Chao took a sword and struck Zuan; Zuan got down from the cart to seize Chao; Chao stabbed Zuan through the breast and ran to Xuande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao snatched a blade, stabbed Lü Zuan through the chest as he leapt from the cart, and fled toward Xuande Hall.

sentences.zh: 川、騰與超格戰，超殺之。

translations.literal: Chuan, Teng, and Chao fought hand to hand; Chao killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chuan and Luo Teng closed with him and died on his sword.

sentences.zh: 纂妻楊氏命禁兵討超，杜尚約兵舍杖。

translations.literal: Zuan's wife Lady Yang ordered the forbidden troops to punish Chao; Du Shang ordered the troops to drop their staves.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang called the guard on Lü Chao, but Du Shang had them stand down.

sentences.zh: 將軍魏益多入，斬纂首以徇曰：「纂違先帝之命，殺害太子，荒耽酒獵，昵近小人，輕害忠良，以百姓為草芥。

translations.literal: General Wei Yiduo entered, beheaded Zuan, and displayed it saying, "Zuan violated the former lord's command, killed the heir apparent, wastefully drowned in wine and hunting, drew near petty men, lightly harmed the loyal and good, and treated the hundred surnames as straw.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yiduo burst in, struck off Lü Zuan's head, and proclaimed, "Lü Zuan broke his father's will, murdered the crown prince, drowned in wine and the chase, trusted villains, slew loyal men, and trampled the people like weeds."

sentences.zh: 番禾太守超以骨肉之親，懼社稷顛覆，已除之矣。

translations.literal: Fanhe prefect Chao, with the closeness of flesh and bone, feared the altars would overturn and therefore removed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fanhe governor Lü Chao, as kinsman, feared the state would fall and removed him.

sentences.zh: 上以安宗廟，下為太子報仇。

translations.literal: Above to secure the ancestral temples, below to avenge the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He acted to steady the shrines and avenge the heir.

sentences.zh: 凡我士庶，同茲休慶。」

translations.literal: All our gentry and commoners share this glad blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Let every subject rejoice in this.

sentences.zh: 偽巴西公呂他、隴西公呂緯時在北城，或說緯曰：「超陵天逆上，士眾不附。

translations.literal: The false Duke of Brazil Lü Ta and Duke of Longxi Lü Wei were then at the north city; someone urged Wei, "Chao defies Heaven and rebels above; soldiers and masses do not attach.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ta and Lü Wei held the north wall when someone told Wei, "Lü Chao has seized power illegally—the army will not follow him."

sentences.zh: 明公以懿弟之親，投戈而起，姜紀、焦辨在南城，楊桓、田誠在東苑，皆我之党也，何慮不濟！

translations.literal: The enlightened lord, with the closeness of a virtuous younger brother, cast down arms and rose; Jiang Ji and Jiao Bian are at the south city, Yang Huan and Tian Cheng are at the east park—all are our faction; what worry that it will not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: You are the virtuous younger brother—raise your spears. Jiang Ji and Jiao Bian hold the south, Yang Huan and Tian Cheng the east park; our allies are everywhere—how can we fail?

sentences.zh: 」緯乃嚴兵謂他曰：「隆、超弑逆，所宜擊之。

translations.literal: Wei thereupon drew up troops and said to Ta, "Long and Chao murdered their lord; they should be struck.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei marshaled men and told Lü Ta, "Lü Long and Lü Chao regicide must be crushed."

sentences.zh: 昔田恆之亂，孔子鄰國之臣，猶抗言於哀公，況今蕭牆有難，而可坐觀乎！

translations.literal: In the Tian Heng turmoil, Confucius, a minister of a neighboring state, still spoke boldly to Duke Ai; how much more when trouble is inside the screen—can one sit and watch!
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Heng seized Qi, Confucius still rebuked his own duke though only a neighbor's minister. Kin are killing kin under our roof—can we watch?

sentences.zh: 」他將從之，他妻梁氏止之曰：「緯、超俱兄弟之子，何為舍超助緯而為禍道乎！

translations.literal: Ta was about to consent; Ta's wife Lady Liang stopped him saying, "Wei and Chao are both brothers' sons—why abandon Chao to help Wei and walk the path of calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ta agreed until his wife said, "Wei and Chao are both nephews—why side with one and invite ruin?"

sentences.zh: 」他謂緯曰：「超事已立，據武庫，擁精兵，圖之為難。

translations.literal: Ta said to Wei, "Chao's affair is already established; he holds the armory and grips crack troops; plotting him is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ta told Lü Wei, "Lü Chao holds the arsenal and picked troops; he is entrenched."

sentences.zh: 且吾老矣，無能為也。

translations.literal: Moreover I am old and can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I am too old for this fight.

sentences.zh: 」超聞，登城告他曰：「纂信讒言，將滅超兄弟。

translations.literal: Chao heard, ascended the city, and told Ta, "Zuan believed slander and was about to destroy Chao's brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao mounted the wall and shouted to Lü Ta, "Lü Zuan meant to wipe us brothers out on rumor."

sentences.zh: 超以身命之切，且懼社稷覆亡，故出萬死之計，為國家唱義，叔父當有以亮之。

translations.literal: Chao, because the urgency of body and life, and moreover fearing the altars' overturn, therefore issued a plan of ten thousand deaths, proclaiming righteousness for the state—uncle should have means to understand.
translations.idiomatic: I risked everything to save the bloodline and the realm—uncle, judge me fairly.

sentences.zh: 」超弟邈有寵於緯，說緯曰：「纂殘國破家，誅戮兄弟，隆、超此舉應天人之心，正欲尊立明公耳。

translations.literal: Chao's younger brother Miao had favor with Wei and said to Wei, "Zuan ruined state and broke family, executed and slaughtered brothers; Long and Chao's act answers the hearts of Heaven and men—it is just that they wish to honor and establish the enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Miao, favored by Lü Wei, whispered, "Lü Zuan shattered the clan. Long and Chao acted for heaven and earth—they mean to set you on the throne."

sentences.zh: 先帝之子，明公為長，四海顒顒，人無異議。

translations.literal: Among the former lord's sons the enlightened lord is eldest; within the four seas all crane their necks; men have no different opinion.
translations.idiomatic: You are the late emperor's eldest surviving son; the realm looks to you alone.

sentences.zh: 隆、超雖不達臧否，終不以孽代宗，更圖異望也，願公勿疑。

translations.literal: Long and Chao, though they do not reach judging good and bad, in the end would not use a bastard branch to replace the main line, nor further plot different hopes; I wish the lord not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: They are no scholars of legitimacy, yet they would never set a junior line above the main house—have no fear.

sentences.zh: 」緯信之，與隆、超結盟，單馬入城，超執而殺之。

translations.literal: Wei believed it, allied with Long and Chao, entered the city on a single horse, and Chao seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei believed him, swore with Long and Chao, rode in alone, and Lü Chao seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，纂嘗與鳩摩羅什棋，殺羅什子，曰：「斫胡奴頭。

translations.literal: Initially Zuan once played chess with Kumarajiva; taking Kumarajiva's piece he said, "Cut off the Hu slave's head.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Zuan played chess with Kumarajiva, captured his piece, and joked, "Off with the barbarian slave's head!"

sentences.zh: 」羅什曰：「不斫胡奴頭，胡奴斫人頭。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva said, "If you do not cut off the Hu slave's head, the Hu slave will cut off men's heads.
translations.idiomatic: The monk answered, "Fail to take the Hu slave's head and the Hu slave will take yours."

sentences.zh: 」超小字胡奴，竟以殺纂。

translations.literal: Chao's childhood name was Hu slave; in the end he killed Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao's pet name was Hu slave—and he slew Lü Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纂在位三年，以元興元年死。

translations.literal: Zuan was on the throne three years and died in the first year of Yuanxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan reigned three years and died in the first year of Yuanxing.

sentences.zh: 隆既篡位，偽諡纂靈皇帝，墓號白石陵。

translations.literal: Long having usurped the throne, falsely posthumously titled Zuan Emperor Ling, tomb name White Stone Mound.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing power, Lü Long gave Lü Zuan the posthumous title Emperor Ling and buried him at the White Stone Tumulus.

sentences.zh: 隆多殺豪望，以立威名，內外囂然，人不自固。

translations.literal: Long greatly killed eminent houses to establish awe name; inside and outside were in uproar; people could not secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long slaughtered leading families to inspire fear; the court and countryside seethed and no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 魏安人焦朗遣使說姚興將姚碩德曰：「呂氏因秦之亂，制命此州。

translations.literal: A man of Weian, Jiao Lang, sent a messenger to persuade Yao Xing's general Yao Shude, "The Lü clan seized command of this province on the turmoil of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Lang of Weian urged Yao Shude, "The Lüs grabbed Liangzhou when Former Qin collapsed."

sentences.zh: 自武皇棄世，諸子兢尋干戈，德刑不恤，殘暴是先，饑饉流亡，死者太半，唯泣訴昊天，而精誠無感。

translations.literal: Since Martial Emperor abandoned the world, the various sons eagerly sought halberds; virtue and punishments were not pitied; cruelty and violence came first; famine and exile; the dead were more than half; only weeping appealed to August Heaven, yet sincere devotion moved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Lü Guang died his sons have torn one another apart, lawless and cruel. Half the people are dead of hunger and flight; prayers to heaven go unheard.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明公道邁前賢，任尊分陝，宜兼弱攻昧，經略此方，救生靈之沈溺，布徽政於玉門。

translations.literal: I humbly consider the enlightened lord's way surpasses former worthies, his commission honors the partition of Shaan; it is fitting to swallow the weak and strike the dark, plan strategy on this side, save the living from drowning, spread fine government to Jade Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue outshines the past and your charge matches the old dukes of Shaan. Strike this weak, benighted state, rescue the drowning people, and carry good rule to the Jade Gate.

sentences.zh: 篡奪之際，為功不難。

translations.literal: At the moment of usurpation, achieving merit is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: They are ripe for the taking.

sentences.zh: 」遣妻子為質。

translations.literal: He sent wife and children as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his family as hostages.

sentences.zh: 碩德遂率眾至姑臧。

translations.literal: Shude thereupon led the host to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shude marched on Guzang.

sentences.zh: 其部將姚國方言於碩德曰：「今懸師三千，後無繼援，師之難也。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Yao Guofang said to Shude, "Now the suspended army is three thousand; behind there is no continuing rescue; this is the army's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guofang warned, "We are three thousand men deep in enemy land with no reserves—that is perilous."

sentences.zh: 宜曜勁鋒，示其威武。

translations.literal: It is fitting to display keen blades and show martial awe.
translations.idiomatic: Flash our steel and show our might.

sentences.zh: 彼以我遠來，必決死距戰，可一舉而平。

translations.literal: They because we came from afar must fight to the death to resist battle; one stroke can pacify.
translations.idiomatic: They will meet us with desperate defense because we came far—one blow can finish it.

sentences.zh: 」碩德從之。

translations.literal: Shude followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shude agreed.

sentences.zh: 呂超出戰，大敗，遁還。

translations.literal: Lü Chao went out to battle, was heavily defeated, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao sallied forth, lost badly, and ran back to the city.

sentences.zh: 隆收集離散，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Long gathered the scattered and ringed the city in firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long rallied stragglers and shut the gates for a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 時熒惑犯帝坐，有群雀鬥于太廟，死者數萬。

translations.literal: At the time Mars encroached on the emperor's seat; flocks of sparrows fought in the Grand Temple; the dead numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Mars trespassed the throne star, sparrows brawled in the imperial temple, and tens of thousands lay dead.

sentences.zh: 東人多謀外叛，將軍魏益多又唱動群心，乃謀殺隆、超，事發，誅之，死者三百餘家。

translations.literal: The eastern men mostly plotted outward rebellion; General Wei Yiduo again stirred the crowd's hearts; they plotted to kill Long and Chao; the matter broke out and they executed them; more than three hundred households died.
translations.idiomatic: Easterners plotted defection; Wei Yiduo fanned the mood; a scheme to murder Lü Long and Lü Chao leaked, and over three hundred families were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣表求與姚興通好，隆弗許。

translations.literal: Thereupon the host of ministers memorialized asking to open good relations with Yao Xing; Long did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The court begged to treat with Yao Xing, but Lü Long refused.

sentences.zh: 呂超諫曰：「通塞有時，艱泰相襲，孫權屈身于魏，譙周勸主迎降，豈非大丈夫哉？

translations.literal: Lü Chao remonstrated, "Open and blocked have their seasons; hardship and ease follow each other; Sun Quan bent his body to Wei; Qiao Zhou urged his lord to welcome surrender—were they not great men?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao argued, "Fortunes turn. Sun Quan bowed to Wei; Qiao Zhou urged surrender—great men bend when they must."

sentences.zh: 勢屈故也。

translations.literal: It is because the situation was bent.
translations.idiomatic: They yielded to necessity.

sentences.zh: 天錫承七世之資，樹恩百載，武旅十萬，謀臣盈朝，秦師臨境，識者導以見機，而愎諫自專，社稷為墟。

translations.literal: Tianxi inherited seven generations' capital, planted favor a hundred years, martial hosts a hundred thousand, strategists filled the court; when Qin troops reached the border, those who saw the moment guided him, yet he stubbornly rejected counsel and monopolized decisions—the altars became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi had seven generations of wealth, a century of goodwill, and a hundred thousand spears, yet when Qin closed in he spurned wise warning and lost everything—a lesson carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 前鑒不遠，我之元龜也。

translations.literal: The former mirror is not far; it is our great tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: That fall is recent history; let it be our oracle.

sentences.zh: 何惜尺書單使，不以危易安！

translations.literal: Why spare a letter and a lone envoy, not to trade peril for safety!
translations.idiomatic: Why not send one letter and one envoy to buy peace?

sentences.zh: 且令卑辭以退敵，然後內修德政，廢興由人，未損大略。

translations.literal: Moreover order humble words to repel the enemy, then within cultivate virtuous government; ruin and rise lie with men—the grand strategy is not yet harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Humble terms can buy a truce; then mend rule at home. Rise or fall is still ours to choose.

sentences.zh: 」隆曰：「吾雖常人，屬當家國之重，不能嗣守成基，保安社稷，以太祖之業委之于人，何面目見先帝於地下！

translations.literal: Long said, "Although I am a common man, I have shouldered the heavy weight of house and state; unable to inherit and guard the accomplished foundation and secure the altars, to entrust Taizu's enterprise to another—what face to see the former lord underground!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long answered, "I am no hero, yet I bear the realm. To hand my father's legacy to a foreign throne—how could I face him beneath the earth?"

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「應龍以屈伸為靈，大人以知機為美。

translations.literal: Chao said, "The responding dragon takes bending and stretching as its spirit; the great man takes knowing the moment as beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao replied, "Dragons thrive by flexing; wise men seize the hour."

sentences.zh: 今連兵積歲，資儲內盡，強寇外逼，百姓嗷然無糊口之寄，假使張、陳、韓、白，亦無如之何！

translations.literal: Now connected arms have piled years; supplies and stores are exhausted within; strong bandits press without; the hundred surnames wail with no hope of a mouthful; suppose Zhang Liang, Chen Ping, Han Xin, and Bai Qi were here—they still could do nothing!
translations.idiomatic: We have fought for years, emptied the granaries, and face foes on every wall while the people starve. Even Zhang Liang or Han Xin could not save us now!

sentences.zh: 陛下宜思權變大綱，割區區常慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should ponder the great pattern of flexible response and cut off petty constant worries.
translations.idiomatic: Think of the larger strategy and shed small scruples.

sentences.zh: 苟卜世有期，不在和好，若天命去矣，宗族可全。

translations.literal: If divination grants the house a span, it lies not in alliance; if Heaven's mandate departs, the clan may yet be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If fate still favors us, peace need not shame us; if doom is sealed, surrender may spare the bloodline.

sentences.zh: 」隆從之，乃請降。

translations.literal: Long followed it; then he asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long relented and sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 碩德表隆為使持節、鎮西大將軍、涼州刺史、建康公。

translations.literal: Shude memorialized Long as Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, Grand General Who Garrisons the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shude had Lü Long named Bearer of the Versatile Insignia, General Who Guards the West, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 於是遣母弟愛子文武舊臣慕容築、楊穎、史難、閻松等五十餘家質于長安，碩德乃還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his mother, younger brother, beloved sons, civil and military old ministers Murong Zhu, Yang Ying, Shi Nan, Yan Song, and more than fifty households as hostages in Chang'an; Shude then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his mother, brothers, sons, and fifty-odd families of old officials—including Murong Zhu, Yang Ying, Shi Nan, and Yan Song—as hostages to Chang'an, after which Yao Shude withdrew.

sentences.zh: 姚興謀臣皆曰：「隆藉伯父余資，制命河外。

translations.literal: Yao Xing's plotting ministers all said, "Long relies on his uncle's leftover resources and commands beyond the River.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's advisers said, "Lü Long still feeds on his uncle's hoard and rules the west."

sentences.zh: 今雖饑窘，尚能自支。

translations.literal: Now although hungry and pressed, he can still support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He is hungry but not broken.

sentences.zh: 若將來豐贍，終非國有。

translations.literal: If in the future he becomes abundant, in the end he will not be the state's possession.
translations.idiomatic: If he recovers, we will never own Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 涼州險絕，世難先違，道清後順，不如因其饑弊而取之。

translations.literal: Liangzhou is perilously cut off; generations hard to defy first, the way clear later compliant—better take it by their hunger and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou is a natural fortress. Strike now while they starve rather than fight them fat.

sentences.zh: 」興乃遣使來觀虛實。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon sent envoys to observe emptiness and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent spies to test their strength.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜又伐隆，隆擊敗之，蒙遜請和結盟，留穀萬餘斛以振饑人。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun again campaigned against Long; Long defeated him; Mengxun asked peace and allied, leaving more than ten thousand hu of grain to relieve the starving.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun attacked again; Lü Long repulsed him; Mengxun sued for peace, swore a pact, and left ten thousand bushels of grain for the hungry.

sentences.zh: 姑臧穀價踴貴，斗直錢五千文，人相食，饑死者十餘萬口。

translations.literal: Grain prices in Guzang leaped; one dou was worth five thousand cash; people ate one another; the starving dead were more than a hundred thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: In Guzang grain hit five thousand cash a peck; cannibalism returned; over a hundred thousand starved.

sentences.zh: 城門盡閉，樵采路絕，百姓請出城乞為夷虜奴婢者日有數百。

translations.literal: City gates were all closed; firewood gathering paths were cut; commoners who begged daily to leave the city to become barbarian slaves numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Every gate stayed shut and fuel ran out; hundreds each day pleaded to be sold to the tribes outside.

sentences.zh: 隆懼沮動人情，盡坑之，於是積屍盈于衛路。

translations.literal: Long feared discouraging human hearts and buried them all in pits; thereupon piled corpses filled the guard roads.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing panic, Lü Long massacred those who wished to flee until the avenues choked with bodies.

sentences.zh: 禿髮傉檀及蒙遜頻來伐之，隆以二寇之逼也，遣超率騎二百，多齎珍寶，請迎于姚興。

translations.literal: Tufa Nutan and Mengxun repeatedly came to campaign against him; Long, because the two bandits pressed, sent Chao leading two hundred horse, bearing many treasures, to request welcome from Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan and Juqu Mengxun kept up the pressure, so Lü Long sent Lü Chao with two hundred horsemen and rich gifts to beg Yao Xing for rescue.

sentences.zh: 興乃遣其將齊難等步騎四萬迎之。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon sent his general Qi Nan and others with forty thousand foot and horse to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Qi Nan with forty thousand men to escort him east.

sentences.zh: 難至姑臧，隆素車白馬迎於道旁。

translations.literal: When Nan reached Guzang, Long in plain cart and white horse welcomed him by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan arrived at Guzang to find Lü Long waiting in a plain cart and white mount.

sentences.zh: 使胤告光廟曰：「陛下往運神略，開建西夏，德被蒼生，威振遐裔。

translations.literal: He sent Yin to announce at Guang's temple, "Your Majesty in former times wielded divine strategy, opened and built Western Xia, virtue covered the black-haired folk, awe shook distant shores.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yin speak at Lü Guang's shrine: "You forged Western Liang, spread kindness, and awed the frontiers."

sentences.zh: 枝嗣不臧，迭相篡弑。

translations.literal: Branch heirs were not good; they repeatedly usurped and murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Your sons and grandsons turned bad and slew one another.

sentences.zh: 二虜交逼，將歸東京，謹與陛下奉訣于此。

translations.literal: Two bandits press together; I am about to return to the eastern capital; I respectfully here with Your Majesty take farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Two foes squeeze us; I must go east to Chang'an and bid your spirit farewell.

sentences.zh: 」歔欷慟泣，酸感興軍。

translations.literal: He sobbed and wept in grief; sour feeling moved Xing's army.
translations.idiomatic: He wept until Yao's soldiers were moved.

sentences.zh: 隆率戶一萬，隨難東遷，至長安，興以隆為散騎常侍，公如故；

translations.literal: Long led ten thousand households and followed Nan eastward; reaching Chang'an, Xing appointed Long Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, duke as before;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long took ten thousand households east with Qi Nan. At Chang'an, Yao Xing named him cavalier attendant and left his ducal title intact;

sentences.zh: 超為安定太守；

translations.literal: Chao became Anding prefect;
translations.idiomatic: he made Lü Chao governor of Anding;

sentences.zh: 文武三十餘人皆擢敘之。

translations.literal: more than thirty civil and military were all promoted and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: and promoted more than thirty of his civil and military followers.

sentences.zh: 其後隆坐與子弼謀反，為興所誅。

translations.literal: Afterward Long sat because he with his son Bi plotted rebellion and was executed by Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Long was executed for plotting revolt with his son Lü Bi.

sentences.zh: 呂光以孝武太元十二年定涼州，十五年僭立，至隆凡十有三載，以安帝元興三年滅。

translations.literal: Lü Guang in Emperor Xiaowu's twelfth year of Taiyuan settled Liangzhou; in the fifteenth year he falsely established; down to Long in all thirteen years; it perished in Emperor An's third year of Yuanxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang took Liangzhou in 387, claimed kingship in 390, and the line ended with Lü Long in 404 after thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自晉室不綱，中原蕩析，苻氏乘釁，竊號神州。

translations.literal: The historian says: From the time the Jin house lost its reins and the central plain shattered, the Fu clan seized the opening and stole the title on the divine continent.
translations.idiomatic: The court historians wrote: Once Jin lost the realm, Fu Jian seized the Central Plain and proclaimed his own rule.

sentences.zh: 世明委質偽朝，位居上將，爰以心膂，受脤遐征。

translations.literal: Shiming pledged himself to the false court, rank reached upper general; as heart and loins he received sacrificial meat on a distant campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang, styled Shiming, served Fu Jian as a top general and led the western expedition as his trusted arm.

sentences.zh: 鐵騎如雲，出玉門而長騖；

translations.literal: Iron cavalry like clouds, out Jade Gate and long gallop;
translations.idiomatic: Iron horsemen streamed beyond the Jade Gate;

sentences.zh: 雕戈耀景，捐金丘而一息。

translations.literal: carved halberds dazzle the sunlight, cast aside golden hills in one breath.
translations.idiomatic: inlaid spears flashed as they swept the sands in a single breath.

sentences.zh: 蕞爾夷陬，承風霧卷，宏圖壯節，亦足稱焉。

translations.literal: The trivial barbarian corner, receiving the wind, rolled up in mist; his grand design and stalwart integrity are also worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: The western tribes folded before him; his ambition and courage deserve mention.

sentences.zh: 屬永固運銷，群雄兢起，班師右地，便有覬覦。

translations.literal: When Yonggu's fortune dissolved and heroes vied to rise, withdrawing the army to the right bank, he then cast covetous eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian fell and warlords rose, Lü Guang drew home his host and eyed the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 於是要結六戎，潛窺雁鼎；

translations.literal: Thereupon he bound the six Rong, secretly peered at the wild-goose cauldron;
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the six tribes and nursed imperial ambition;

sentences.zh: 併吞五郡，遂假鴻名。

translations.literal: swallowed five commanderies, then borrowed a great name.
translations.idiomatic: seized five commanderies, then took a kingly title.

sentences.zh: 控黃河以設險，負玄漠而為固，自謂克昌霸業，貽厥孫謀。

translations.literal: He controlled the Yellow River to set peril, shouldered the dark desert to be firm; he himself claimed thriving hegemony and bequeathed plans to grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Yellow River as a moat and the Gobi as a shield, sure his line would flourish for generations.

sentences.zh: 尋而耄及政昏，親離眾叛，瞑目甫爾，釁發蕭牆。

translations.literal: Soon old age arrived and government darkened, kin left and masses rebelled; his eyes had barely closed when trouble burst within the screen.
translations.idiomatic: Age and misrule followed; kin fled and the people turned. He had hardly died before brothers drew knives.

sentences.zh: 紹、纂凡才，負乘致寇；

translations.literal: Shao and Zuan were ordinary talents; bearing the ride brought bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao and Lü Zuan were mediocrity; seizing power invited ruin;

sentences.zh: 弘、超凶狡，職為亂階；

translations.literal: Hong and Chao were fierce and cunning, their office the step of disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong and Lü Chao were cruel and sly, the very authors of chaos;

sentences.zh: 永基庸庸，面縛姚氏。

translations.literal: Yongji was commonplace, bound and delivered to the Yao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long, styled Yongji, was feeble and ended bound before Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 昔竇融歸順，榮煥累葉；

translations.literal: Formerly Dou Rong submitted to the Han and his glory blazed for generations;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong once yielded to Han and his house shone for ages;

sentences.zh: 隗囂幹紀，靡終身世。

translations.literal: Wei Xiao resisted the mandate and met no peaceful end in life.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao defied heaven and died without peace.

sentences.zh: 而光棄茲勝躅，遵彼覆車，十數年間，終致殘滅。

translations.literal: Yet Guang abandoned that winning track and followed that overturned cart; within a dozen years he ended in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang spurned the wise path and copied failures, destroying himself within a decade.

sentences.zh: 向使矯邪歸正，革偽為忠，鳴檄而蕃晉朝，仗義而誅醜虜，則燕、秦之地可定，桓、文之功可立，郭黁、段業豈得肆其奸，蒙遜、烏孤無所窺其隙矣。

translations.literal: Had he straightened wickedness to return to rectitude, changed false to loyal, raised a proclamation to serve the Jin court and wielded righteousness to punish the ugly barbarians, then Yan and Qin lands could have been settled, Huan and Wen's merit could have been raised—how could Guo Nen and Duan Ye have unleashed their treachery, how could Mengxun and Wuguji have spied their gaps!
translations.idiomatic: Had he turned loyal to Jin and marched against the real foes, he might have matched Huan Wen's fame and kept rebels from rising.

sentences.zh: 而猥竊非據，何其謬哉！

translations.literal: Yet vulgarly he stole illegitimate position—how absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Instead he seized an unlawful throne—a gross mistake.

sentences.zh: 夫天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。

translations.literal: The great virtue of Heaven and earth is called life; the great treasure of the sage is called position.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's chief gift is life; the sage's chief prize is the throne.

sentences.zh: 非其人而處其位者，其禍必速；

translations.literal: One who is not that person yet occupies that position—his calamity will be swift;
translations.idiomatic: The wrong man on the throne invites swift disaster;

sentences.zh: 在其位而忘其德者，其殃必至。

translations.literal: one who occupies that position yet forgets that virtue—his punishment will surely arrive.
translations.idiomatic: the right seat without virtue brings certain punishment.

sentences.zh: 天鑒非遠，庸可濫乎！

translations.literal: Heaven's mirror is not far; how can one recklessly abuse it!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven watches closely—do not trifle with its charge!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金行不兢，寶業斯屯。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The metal line did not prevail; the precious enterprise thus halted.
translations.idiomatic: Epitaph: Jin's metal mandate faltered; the sacred work stalled.

sentences.zh: 瓜分九寓，沴聚三秦。

translations.literal: The nine domains split like a melon; misfortune gathered in three Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The realm split apart; calamity clung to the three Qin heartland.

sentences.zh: 呂氏伺隙，欺我人神。

translations.literal: The Lü clan watched for openings and deceived our people and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Lüs seized their chance and cheated men and gods.

sentences.zh: 天命難假，終亦傾淪。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is hard to borrow; in the end they also toppled and sank.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate cannot be stolen; they fell at last.
